research.abstract: Summary Despite a century of BCG use, tuberculosis remains a leading cause of death from infectious diseases and more effective vaccines are urgently needed. Here, we combined antigen discovery in zebrafish with mRNA vaccine technology to generate multivalent vaccine candidates, TUmRNA 4 , TUmRNA 6 and TUmRNA 9 , encoding four, six, or nine Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens, respectively. The vaccines were well tolerated and induced robust antigen-specific cellular immune responses, including IFNγ production and expansion of memory T-cell populations. In mice, TUmRNA 4 and TUmRNA 6 reduced pulmonary M. tuberculosis burden and lung pathology to levels comparable to BCG vaccination, and TUmRNA 6 enhanced BCG-mediated protection when administered as a booster vaccine. In guinea pigs, TUmRNA 9 reduced bacterial burden in the lungs, spleen, and lymph nodes and decreased pulmonary lesions. These findings demonstrate that protective antigens identified in zebrafish can be translated into effective multivalent mRNA vaccines and establish a framework for tuberculosis vaccine development across multiple preclinical models.

research.abstract: Abstract The deep-learning language model offers promising approaches to molecular design. However, existing models typically exhibit one or more of the following limitations: structural constraints, confinement to a single task, and lack of cross-domain capability (e.g., protein-to-ligand generation). Inspired by GPT’s success in language modeling, we introduce ProLigGPT, a seq2seq autoregressive model based on GPT-2 and trained on ∼1.9 million protein-ligand pairs without 3D structures. ProLigGPT supports tasks including de novo ligand generation and scaffold-based molecular design for target proteins. Benchmarking against three state-of-the-art structure-based models across eight representative target proteins, ProLigGPT demonstrated superior performance on comprehensive metrics. Through systematic evaluations of ProLigGPT’s interpretability, we find that ProLigGPT uses the full protein sequence to generate target-aware ligands, unlike pocket-based strategies that depend only on residues near the binding site. Applying ProLigGPT to Pl3Kα inhibitor design successfully yielded inhibitors with a novel scaffold and inhibitors derived from a known scaffold, demonstrating that ProLigGPT can reach beyond the boundaries of known chemical space. Finally, we validated the generalization ability of ProLigGPT on Target T1, which lacks a crystal structure and known inhibitors, confirming that ProLigGPT can design inhibitors solely from sequence information. These findings highlight the promise of language models in designing ligands for target proteins free from structural constraints, offering a flexible and scalable framework for exploring vast chemical spaces in drug discovery.

research.abstract: Abstract All cellular life possesses environmental interfaces like cell membranes or cell walls, yet the compositional complexity of these major cell components limits structural and evolutionary studies. Prokaryotic surface layer (S-layer) exoskeletons, with their homopolymer paracrystalline architecture, offer a more tractable model of an environmental interface. However, extreme sequence diversity and heterogeneous multidomain organisation of S-layer proteins confound conventional evolutionary analyses. Here, by combining phylogenomics with structural modelling, we show that extensive sequence divergence, modular evolution and lateral gene transfer drive lineage-specific S-layer diversification across both monoderm ( Bacillaceae , Peptostreptococcaceae ) and diderm ( Caulobacteraceae , Deinococcaceae ) bacteria. Focusing on the Gram-positive order Peptostreptococcales , including environmental isolates and clinical pathogens, we uncover multiple S-layer architectures conferring divergent physiological properties. Molecular microbiology reveals that among close relatives utilising the same exoskeleton type, only pathogens display resistance to the antimicrobial immune effectors LL-37 and lysozyme. Furthermore, by experimentally determining two S-layer structures, we unravel how mechanisms including (intra)domain gains and losses generate hyper-diversity of homologous S-layers among clinical isolates of the pathogen Clostridioides difficile . Our findings establish the S-layer as a paradigm of molecular modularity and evolutionary plasticity. Specifically, evolution of a single structural protein enables rapid cell-surface reconfiguration and contributes to immune evasion in bacterial pathogens.

research.abstract: Codon usage bias is a fundamental genomic characteristic that prefers non-random preferential use of synonymous codons. It is a major determinant of translational efficiency, gene regulation, and molecular evolution. However, the evolutionary bias and functional relevance of codon usage bias across the plant lineage is poorly defined and yet to understand what are the major factors responsible for relative synonymous codon usage (RSCU) in genomes and how codon usage bias influences the gene regulation, molecular evolution genomes. A genome-wide codon usage bias study of coding DNA sequences of 262 plant genome was conducted. It encompassed more than 4.6 billion codons from > 11 million coding sequences. Relative synonymous codon usage, codon adaptation index, codon-anticodon mapping, effective number of codon (ENC)-GC3, GC1,2-GC3, parity rule 2 (PR2-bias), molecular economy, and machine learning approaches were used for the study. It was found that codon usage bias was strongly non-random and exhibited a clear phylogenetic structuring. The higher plants favoured A/T-ending, whereas early-diverging lineages were enriched in G/C-ending codons. Analysis of RSCU, codon adaptation index, and codon-anticodon pairing indicated that translational selection is mediated by tRNA availability, contributing sustainability to these molecular patterns. Machine-learning approaches identified a small subset of codons having outsized influence on genome-wide codon usage landscapes. Further studies revealed the presence of robust inverse relationships between the effective number of codons and GC content at synonymous third positions. Neutrality analysis revealed approximately 61% of variation was driven by mutational pressure, tempered by selective constraints. Phylogenetic reconstruction showed a progressive relaxation of codon bias from algae to angiosperms while maintaining a conserved molecular economy cost of ~ 30 ATP per codon across the lineages. The study revealed codon usage bias is lineage-specific evolutionary conserved trait governed by mutation, selection, and translational optimization.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide important cardiorenal benefits in chronic kidney disease (CKD), but their effects on vascular calcification remain conflicting. Whether potential anti-calcifying effects are shared across gliflozins or involve mechanisms beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition is unknown. Methods We systematically compared canagliflozin, dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in a high-phosphate diet-induced mouse model of vascular calcification and complementary ex vivo and in vitro models, including rodent and human vascular tissues and vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Aortic transcriptional response was investigated by RNA sequencing. VSMC calcification, proliferation, migration, viability, glucose uptake and bioenergetics were investigated using complementary cellular assays, including OsteoSense staining, Annexin V/propidium iodide staining, radiolabeled 2-deoxyglucose uptake and Seahorse ATP rate analysis. SGLT2/1 expression was examined by RT-qPCR, Western blotting and immunofluorescence. We also evaluated sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, and mizagliflozin, a selective SGLT1 inhibitor. Results Among the three gliflozins, only canagliflozin significantly reduced aortic calcification in vivo . Its anti-calcifying effect was also observed in rodent aortic rings, human vascular explants, cultured VSMCs and aortic rings from diabetic db/db mice. Aortic RNA-seq revealed that canagliflozin partially reversed HPD-induced transcriptional alterations, including changes in pro-calcific signaling and cellular metabolism, while some endothelial and inflammatory responses were shared among gliflozins. In mouse VSMCs, canagliflozin reduced calcification across all tested concentrations, dose-dependently decreased osteogenic marker expression, and reduced proliferation and migration. Increased apoptotic and damaged cell fractions were observed at higher concentrations, but not at lower concentrations. Canagliflozin also reduced glucose uptake and mitochondrial ATP production, without significantly affecting glycolytic ATP production. Neither dapagliflozin nor empagliflozin reproduced these cellular and metabolic effects at any of the concentrations tested. SGLT2 and SGLT1 expression was low or undetectable in vascular tissues and cells, and neither sotagliflozin nor mizagliflozin reproduced the anti-calcifying effect of canagliflozin in vivo or in vitro . Conclusions Canagliflozin exhibits a selective anti-calcifying profile among the gliflozins tested, associated with changes in VSMC responses and cellular metabolism. These findings suggest that its vascular protective effects may involve mechanisms beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition.

research.abstract: Estimating the effective sample size (ESS) is fundamental in Bayesian phylogenetic inference to account for autocorrelation in MCMC samples. While methods for continuous parameters are well established, the discrete and high-dimensional nature of treespace poses substantial challenges. In this paper, we introduce a new approach based on Conditional Clade Distributions (CCDs) to emulate MCMC chains with known ESS bounds. We compare existing tree ESS estimators with novel approaches that utilize CCDs as tractable tree distributions, as well as a new probabilistic estimator based on differences in clade frequencies between independent chains. Using our emulated chains from both simulated and real datasets, we assess estimators for their ability to recover the true ESS (accuracy), their insensitivity to the removal of autocorrelated samples from the chain (stability), and their tolerance to combining multiple chains together (robustness). We further examine how multimodality and poor inter-mode chain mixing can compromise the reliability of tree ESS estimates. These findings indicate that our new CCD-based estimators perform comparably to existing approaches with respect to accuracy, stability, and robustness. In contrast, the probabilistic estimator and two previously recommended methods incur prohibitive computational costs for long chains. Together, these results establish a new framework for evaluating tree ESS estimators using CCD-based emulated MCMC chains and demonstrate their performance and current limitations in practical phylogenetic analyses. The expanded suite of tree ESS estimators is available in the user-friendly TreeStat2 software package for BEAST 2.

research.abstract: Most signals from genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of complex traits implicate noncoding variants with putative gene regulatory effects. However, currently identified regulatory variants, particularly expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), explain only a small fraction of GWAS associations. Moreover, GWAS loci are enriched near evolutionarily constrained genes, whereas constrained genes are depleted of detectable eQTLs, suggesting that weak or context-specific regulatory mechanisms may contribute substantially to disease risk but remain poorly captured by existing approaches. Here, we introduce scHINT (single-cell gene expression Heritability estimation with genotype x context INTeraction), a computationally efficient framework for quantifying cell-level expression heritability and context-dependent genetic regulation from large-scale single-cell data. Applying scHINT to human brain single-nucleus RNA-seq data, we found that genotype-by-cell-state heritability was widespread across brain cell types and, on average, exceeded main genetic heritability, indicating that context-dependent genetic effects explain a substantial fraction of heritable expression variation. GxCell-State heritability was enriched among low-frequency variants and constrained genes, and showed stronger enrichment for functional gene sets and disease heritability than main genetic effects. Using a novel GxCell-State TWAS framework, we identified 68% more disease-risk genes and recapitulated rare-variant burden-test gene TREM2, which was missed by state-agnostic TWAS. In blood, we observed the same direction of enrichment for GxCell-State heritability at constrained genes, but weaker than in brain, suggesting that cell-state-dependent regulation at constrained genes may be more prominent in brain. Finally, extending scHINT to perturbation screens revealed substantial perturbation-by-cell-state effects, highlighting broad context dependence in transcriptional responses.

research.abstract: Objective Evidence on inpatient-related costs for tuberculosis (TB) patients remains limited for Southwest China. This study used quantile regression to explore factors associated with inpatient expenditures among TB patients treated at a designated infectious-disease hospital in Guizhou Province, Southwest China. Methods Baseline characteristics and inpatient cost data of TB patients admitted to a designated infectious disease hospital in Guizhou Province from January 2018 to December 2024 were retrospectively collected. Quantile regression models were applied to identify determinants of inpatient costs across different cost distributions. Results The findings showed that, at lower cost quantiles, self pay patients had lower inpatient costs (10th percentile; coefficient = -141.79). Conversely, patients covered by social basic medical insurance had significantly lower inpatient costs at higher cost quantiles (90th percentile; coefficient = -97 404.08). Manual labor workers and retirees had higher inpatient costs across the 10th to 90th percentiles compared with other occupational groups. Inpatient length of stay, receipt of interventional procedures, drug resistance, admission status, and comorbidities were positively associated with inpatient costs across the 10th to 90th percentiles (all P < 0.001). Cost differences existed across quantiles for different TB types: disseminated TB produced the highest costs at the 10th percentile (coefficient = 1367.35), while tuberculous meningitis incurred the highest costs from the 50th to the 90th percentiles. According to the relative importance ranking, the most influential factors (in descending order) were length of stay, admission status, TB type, procedural intervention, and occupational factors. Conclusion Based on seven year consecutive inpatient data, this study indicates that TB inpatient expenditures are affected by multiple factors and differ across cost quantiles. Targeted cost containment strategies should be developed according to patient characteristics to reduce medical expenses and shorten hospital stays without impairing treatment outcomes. These findings provide theoretical evidence for formulating TB cost control policies for similar hospital settings. Caution should be exercised when generalizing these results to all TB patients across Southwest China given the single center study design.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections in bronchiectasis airways result in poorer lung function, advanced lung lobe involvement, worsened life quality, and higher hospitalisation rates. Despite high prevalence, little is known about P. aeruginosa population genomics, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) rates, persistence, and transmission dynamics in Australians with bronchiectasis. Methods P. aeruginosa ( n= 137) isolated between 2009 and 2025 from 59 Australians with bronchiectasis underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing against 11 antipseudomonal drugs, whole-genome sequencing, comparative genomics, and in silico AMR determinant identification. Data were integrated with 4,575 publicly available bronchiectasis-derived P. aeruginosa genomes to determine global phylogenomic and AMR determinant patterns. Results High AMR rates were identified in the Australian isolates, with 75.9% resistant to at least one antimicrobial, 19.7% multidrug-resistant, and 9.5% extremely drug-resistant. AMR rates were highest (64.2%) for ciprofloxacin and cefepime (44.5%), and lowest for piperacillin/tazobactam (8.8%) and colistin (0.7%). Phylogenomics uncovered several instances of within-host evolution, hypermutation, persistence, and multi-lineage infections. Of the fifty-seven identified multilocus sequence types (STs), seven (12.3%) were novel, five were high-risk international clones (ST274 [6.6%], ST395 [0.7%], ST244 [0.7%], ST277 [0.7%], ST298 [0.7%]) and three were common global clones (ST253 [5.1%], ST155 [3.6%], ST260 [0.7%]). No high-risk AMR-conferring mobile genetic elements were seen, although numerous chromosomal AMR determinants were identified. AMR determinant prevalence was consistent with the global dataset, with no evidence of geographic clustering. Conclusions Our study provides critical insights into P. aeruginosa diversity in Australians with bronchiectasis. High AMR rates and chronic colonisation highlight the need to improve diagnostics, antimicrobial stewardship measures, and infection control practices in this neglected clinical cohort.

research.abstract: Abstract Background TB eradication strategies in high burden countries need affordable, scalable, and accessible screening tools. This study investigated the diagnostic accuracy of C-reactive protein (CRP), serum amyloid A (SAA), and interferon gamma-induced protein 10 (IP-10) as potential screening tools. Method This cross-sectional diagnostic study investigated stored archived serum samples from three groups of subjects; bacteriology confirmed symptomatic TB group (n=57), probable TB (n=56) and healthy controls (n=60). CRP and SAA concentrations were measured using near point-of-care fluorescence immunoassay (NPOCT-FIA), while IP-10 was measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Diagnostic performance of individual and combined biomarkers was evaluated Results Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance of serum amyloid A (SAA) and C-reactive protein (CRP) for identifying confirmed tuberculosis (TB). Compared with probable TB and healthy controls, SAA achieved an AUC of 0.961 (cut-off > 31.0 mg/L), with 96.5% sensitivity and 88.6% specificity, while CRP achieved an AUC of 0.953 (cut-off 21.3 mg/L), with 96.5% sensitivity and 86.0% specificity. Interferon gamma-induced protein 10 (IP-10) showed poor discrimination (AUC 0.545). Combined CRP and SAA achieved 100.0% sensitivity and 83.3% specificity. Conclusion SAA and CRP met WHO target product profile criteria for TB triage screening.

research.abstract: Abstract Tarsiers, an elusive family of primates found in Indonesia and the Philippines, sit at an essential point in primate evolution, with their divergence between that of Strepsirrhini (lemurs) and Simiiformes (monkeys and apes). Through homology searches, we have discovered that tarsiers carry the first known case in primates of a gene expansion of protein kinase R (PKR), a kinase involved in the response to viral infection. PKR was quadruplicated in the ancestor of tarsiers and has been maintained since then in all sequenced tarsier species. The extra copies lack the double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) binding domains necessary for detecting viral infection yet largely maintain the residues necessary for the kinase function that carries out PKR’s antiviral function. We show that three of the four PKR copies indeed maintain kinase activity, one of which appears to be resistant to the viral PKR antagonist K3 from vaccinia virus. Our analyses of site and branch-site positive selection reveal that the tarsier PKRs are under positive selection. We propose that these extra copies could serve as a diversification strategy to bypass viral inhibitors that bind PKR’s kinase domain, or they could alternatively serve as decoys that shield the canonical PKR from viral inhibition. This is the first instance of mammal PKR duplicates lacking dsRNA-binding domains and may highlight an innovation in an ancient, long-standing molecular arms race between viruses and a close relative of humans.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Catalogues of genetic variants associated with resistance underpin whole-genome sequencing (WGS)- based predictions of drug susceptibility in Mycobacterium tuberculosis , and are essential for developing molecular diagnostics and surveillance. The current gold standard catalogues are those released by the WHO but the underlying data are neither fully available nor straightforward to interpret. Open and reproducible methods would help address these problems, extending the important work already done to better prepare for implementation into readily updatable surveillance platforms. Methods We have developed an automated method, catomatic , that uses a binomial test to associate informative isolates with resistance or susceptibility, and built a catalogue ( catomatic-1 ) from the same 39,358 samples used to construct the first edition of the WHO catalogue ( WHOv1 ). We performed a sensitivity analysis to optimise the statistical and bioinformatic parameters for each drug, and benchmarked catomatic-1 against WHOv1 using a hold-out Validation Dataset of 14,380 isolates. Findings By using simpler statistics, catomatic-1 algorithmically classified 1,329 genetic variants, ranging from five for linezolid to 440 for pyrazinamide. WHOv1 included generalisable rules added by a panel of experts, increasing its predictive coverage, but at the cost of automation and deterministic reproducibility. Despite not including such expert rules, catomatic-1 achieves comparable performance for all drugs, with sensitivities for first-line agents above 88% on the hold-out Validation Dataset. The automated process allowed us to efficiently explore parameter space; for instance, detecting resistance-associated variants with low read support improved the sensitivity for all drugs. Interpretation Performant resistance catalogues for M. tuberculosis can be built automatically and reproducibly using transparent statistical methods. As more data are collected, catalogue content and performance will evolve, highlighting the need for proper versioning, machine/human readability, and open access. This approach demonstrates resistance catalogues used in surveillance (and potentially diagnostics) can be rapidly and reproducibly updated. Funding The National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), Engineering and Physics Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), the Ellison Institute of Technology (EIT), Oxford Ltd and ORACLE Corporation. Research in context Evidence before this study We searched PubMed and preprint servers (bioRxiv, medRxiv), and publicly available mutation catalogues for studies linking Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomic variants with drug resistance using whole-genome or targeted sequencing and phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing (pDST). Search terms combined “Mycobacterium tuberculosis”, “genome sequencing”, “mutation catalogue”, ”mutation effects”, “drug resistance”, and individual drug names, with no language or date restriction. We included studies providing paired, clinical genomic and pDST or MIC data, excluding purely in silico or case-only reports. This work directly builds on methodologies and data published by five prior studies, including our previous work that introduced our method by applying it to a single drug (bedaquiline), and makes primary comparisons with the First ( WHOv1 ) and Second (WHOv2) Editions of the WHO Catalogue of mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis . Added value of this study Historically, catalogues of resistance mutations in M. tuberculosis have been built by combining rules derived from statistical association testing, the literature and the views of experts with the aim of maximising performance. As the sizes of the datasets used to train such catalogues has increased, the relative contributions of each of these sources to performance has shifted. The current gold standard is WHOv2 which applies a conservative statistical association framework to each genetic variant; this approach is well-suited to molecular test design as classifications are unlikely to change with more data but is less appropriate for surveillance of antimicrobial resistance, which requires predictions that directly reflect the underlying data and can be readily updated and systematically parsed. We developed catomatic , an open source tool for reproducibly building catalogues of resistance-associated genetic variants. Trained on the same samples used to build WHOv1 and benchmarked on a hold-out Validation Dataset, catomatic achieves comparable definite prediction rates, sensitivity and specificity to WHOv1 without expert-rule augmentation and despite using simpler statistics. Here we establish it can be used to build a catalogue for multiple antibiotics by introducing per-drug parameter optimisation, thereby demonstrating applicability across diverse resistance mechanisms. It produces machine-readable outputs (CSV/JSON), and we demonstrate that lowering read-support thresholds can improve detection of minor resistance subpopulations. Implications of all the available evidence Catalogues of resistance-associated variants for M. tuberculosis can be rapidly and transparently constructed. Making catalogues available in human/machine-readable formats with uncertainty estimates will improve uptake of WGS for M. tuberculosis surveillance and diagnostics; using a reproducible process permits diagnostic test manufacturers, researchers, clinical and public health laboratories to select the level of statistical support necessitated by their specific use-case. Policymakers should balance the benefits of expert rules against loss of automation and end-to-end reproducibility. Future work will expand the size of the datasets used, integrate minimum inhibitory concentration data, and establish consensus workflows for routine, transparent catalogue updates.

research.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) remains the most economically devastating pathogen of the global swine industry, with frequent genetic recombination and continuous lineage replacement driving its rapid evolution. Hubei Province, a major swine-producing hub in central China, endures substantial PRRSV disease pressure, yet the current epidemiological and evolutionary landscape of circulating strains remains poorly characterized. In this study, 1478 clinical samples were collected from 12 prefecture-level cities between 2024 and 2025 and subjected to RT-PCR detection, ORF5 sequencing, virus isolation, and complete genome analysis. The detection rate among clinical samples was 26.32%, highest in nursery pigs (32.65%). Phylogenetic analysis of 136 ORF5 sequences revealed lineage 1 dominance (66.18%), comprising NADC30-like (38.24%) and NADC34-like (27.94%) strains, followed by lineage 8 (24.26%), lineage 5 (5.15%), and lineage 3 (4.41%). Six isolates were recovered, and whole-genome analysis identified lineage-specific NSP2 deletion patterns and a recombinant strain (LW HP) bearing a JXA1-like backbone with NADC30-like insertions. Selection pressure analysis ranked Nsp2 as the least-constrained gene (dN/dS = 0.3065; purifying selection), with positively selected codons in GP5 and the NSP2 hypervariable region. These findings delineate the current epidemic status and genetic characteristics of PRRSV in central China, providing critical data for regional prevention and vaccine development.

research.abstract: Background Loss to follow-up (LTFU) during tuberculosis treatment is a major programmatic gap, but how much excess mortality it causes has been difficult to estimate, because individuals who disengage differ from those who do not, and they must survive long enough to be recorded as having disengaged. Quantifying this excess and identifying which populations are at greatest risk are critical to informing program design and resource allocation. Methods and findings We followed 171,048 people aged 15 years or older starting a first course of tuberculosis treatment in São Paulo State, Brazil, between 2013 and 2023, linking surveillance and mortality registries; 20,830 (12.2%) were LTFU, defined as interruption of treatment for at least 30 consecutive days. Among those LTFU, 65% had received directly observed therapy (DOT). Using a clone-censor-weight target trial emulation, we contrasted two strategies over 60 months from the first day of treatment: disengagement at any point during the first 6 months and remaining in care throughout. Analyses were adjusted for age, sex, race, education, HIV status, diabetes, alcohol use, drug use, incarceration, homelessness, hospitalization at diagnosis, clinical form of tuberculosis, DOT, and municipality. A rolling landmark analysis addressed the timing of disengagement and cause-specific mortality excess. LTFU increased standardized 5-year mortality by 2.49 percentage points (95% CI [1.94, 3.17]). In a rolling landmark analysis, tuberculosis accounted for 61% of the 5-year excess mortality. Relative effects were largest in younger, stably housed individuals, whose baseline mortality was low; the largest absolute excess fell on people living with HIV (5.16 percentage points, 95% CI [3.76, 6.60]). The excess was similar for disengagement at any point in the first 4 months of treatment and attenuated thereafter. Limitations include the absence from the registry of severity markers such as radiographic extent and bacillary load, so residual confounding cannot be excluded. Conclusions Despite high DOT coverage, disengagement during the first 6 months of tuberculosis treatment was common and increased 5-year mortality under the stated identification assumptions, with the excess concentrated in deaths attributed to tuberculosis. Interventions that provide support throughout treatment should be tested for their effectiveness in sustaining engagement and reducing mortality.

Up to 80% of TBM patients develop hydrocephalus, and outcomes in advanced disease are determined primarily by the timing of anti-tuberculous therapy (ATT) rather than the method of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) diversion. We report a fatal case of isolated CNS tuberculosis (TB) complicated by aqueductal stenosis-induced obstructive hydrocephalus, in which a systemic diagnostic delay, driven by the requirement for microbiological confirmation before ATT could be dispensed, cascaded into delayed medical and surgical management and was the principal determinant of outcome rather than surgical technique. Case Description: A 26-year-old human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-negative Egyptian male presented with recurrent high-grade fever, neck stiffness, diplopia, and urinary retention. CSF showed high protein (306.7 mg/ dL), low glucose (42.1 mg/dL), and lymphocytic pleocytosis (400 cells/mm 3 ), with negative Ziehl–Neelsen stain and BioFire ME panel, which does not include Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB). Despite a CSF profile suggestive of TBM, GeneXpert MTB/rifampicin Ultra was not performed and ATT was deferred pending polymerase chain reaction confirmation. Dexamethasone was started appropriately on day 1. Computed tomography (CT) brain showed ventricular dilatation, but neurosurgical consultation was not obtained. CT chest later showed no pulmonary involvement, supporting isolated CNS TB. On Day 5, the patient deteriorated to Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 6–7 with seizures; emergency external ventricular drain (EVD) was inserted and ATT initiated on day 6, approximately 36 days after symptom onset. He subsequently developed steroid-induced diabetic ketoacidosis and severe hypernatremia consistent with central diabetes insipidus. Despite EVD and ATT, neurological status progressed to GCS 2T with absent brainstem reflexes, and he died approximately 10 days after EVD insertion. Conclusion: This case illustrates three critical failures: (1) neurosurgical consultation was reactive rather than proactive – initiated upon seizures and coma rather than upon CT evidence of hydrocephalus; (2) CSF diversion without concurrent ATT is temporizing, not curative – ongoing meningeal inflammation will progress regardless of EVD adequacy; and (3) a negative syndromic molecular panel that lacks MTB coverage must not delay empirical ATT when the CSF profile is unambiguous. The EVD was technically appropriate and correctly positioned; the therapeutic window had already closed before surgery was performed. In Medical Research Council Grade III TBM, outcome is determined by ATT timing and disease severity at presentation, not by the specific method of CSF diversion.

research.abstract: Introduction A substantial proportion of people with tuberculosis (TB) do not experience or report typical symptoms. We aimed to describe the characteristics of people with asymptomatic TB disease (aTB) and compare its proportion among people diagnosed with TB during community-wide active case finding (ACF) and passive case finding (PCF) in Vietnam. Methods We undertook a cohort study in Ca Mau Province, Vietnam, comparing people with pulmonary TB detected through community-wide ACF using rapid molecular testing irrespective of symptoms, and those diagnosed through routine care at district health facilities (PCF) over the same period. We defined aTB as TB disease without symptoms, based on a post-diagnosis questionnaire. Secondary analyses applied alternative aTB definitions: absence of WHO 4-symptoms and cough for ≥2 weeks. We used modified Poisson regression with robust sandwich variance to quantify the prevalence ratio for aTB in ACF versus PCF. Results Asymptomatic disease was present in 0.9% (PCF) and 12.9% (ACF) of people diagnosed with TB. People with aTB showed lower culture positivity and Xpert Mycobacterium tuberculosis/rifampicin semi-quantitative levels. However, >70% had chest X-ray findings consistent with TB. Compared to PCF, ACF-detected cases were more likely to lack symptoms under each definition: adjusted prevalence ratios for aTB were 13.7 [95%CI 3.2-58.7] for asymptomatic, 2.6 [95%CI 1.6-4.5] for WHO 4-symptoms, and 1.9 [95%CI 1.3-2.8] for cough ≥2 weeks. Conclusion Community-wide ACF detected a significantly higher proportion of aTB than PCF. Screening strategies that require symptoms as a prerequisite are likely to miss a substantial proportion of people with TB.

research.abstract: DEG (Degradation of periplasmic proteins) proteases are ATP-independent serine endopeptidases found in bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes including plants. They are considered to be key regulators of development and stress tolerance in plants. In this study, a comprehensive genome-wide analysis identified 19 serine protease-like DEG family proteins in potato (Solanum tuberosum L.), revealing their structural diversity, domain architecture, and regulatory potential. Physiochemical profiling showed a predominance of acidic isoelectric points (pI), variable protein lengths (169–1083 amino acids), and differential stability indices. Subcellular localization predicted most DEG proteases to reside in the chloroplast, with others distributed across cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, and peroxisome. Domain analysis confirmed the universal presence of the trypsin domain, with varying numbers of PDZ domains and additional conserved motifs among paralogs. Evolutionary divergence analysis of StDEG genes and their orthologs from six Solanaceae species as well as Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa, and Zea mays revealed dN/dS ratios below one for all orthologous pairs, suggesting that StDEG genes have evolved under strong purifying selection and remained highly conserved throughout plant evolution. Gene ontology annotations linked DEG proteases to key biological functions including PSII repair, photoinhibition, and chloroplast organization, alongside protein catabolism and light stimulus response. Promoter analysis revealed an abundance of cis-regulatory elements (CREs), particularly light-responsive motifs, along with hormone and stress-related elements such as ABRE, ARE, and MBS. Expression profiling across eight developmental tissues demonstrated tissue-specific expression patterns, with strong transcript accumulation of selected DEG members in senescent leaf, stolon, shoot apex, and tuber. Interestingly, several splice variants showed unique expression dynamics, including stage-specific and stress-induced activation. Upon exposure to abiotic and hormonal cues, 16 DEG proteases displayed significant transcriptional modulation, particularly under light, ABA, and Zeatin treatments, with notable fold changes reaching up to 26-fold in certain variants. These findings highlight the functional versatility of DEG proteases in potato development and stress adaptation, especially their responsiveness to light and hormonal stimuli. The characterization of these proteases paves the way for future studies on their roles in crop resilience and genome editing applications.

research.abstract: The family Noctuidae includes agricultural pests that vary in geographic distribution and host range. This study analyzed 30 mitogenomes representing 14 noctuid species; Ostrinia nubilalis (Crambidae) served as the phylogenetic outgroup. The genomes contained the typical complement of 37 mitochondrial genes and exhibited conserved gene order, pronounced A + T enrichment, and a preference for A/T-ending synonymous codons. A neutrality regression based on species means revealed a modest positive association between GC3 and GC12 (R 2 = 0.3201; p = 0.03494), although it could not distinguish the respective contributions of mutation and selection. Maximum-likelihood and Bayesian analyses of 13 protein-coding genes (11,229 bp) agreed on 26 of the 28 internal groupings in the maximum-likelihood tree, including a strongly supported Spodoptera clade. Differences in deeper relationships occurred at nodes with limited support. All 13 genes had dN/dS estimates below one (0.00306-0.01691), consistent with purifying selection. Codon usage varied among gene categories, and gene-wise codon bias was not significantly associated with dN/dS. Five crop-associated species with multiple larval host plants and documented long-distance migration- Helicoverpa armigera, Athetis lepigone, Spodoptera litura, S. frugiperda, and Mamestra brassicae -fell below the fitted neutrality regression line. Whether their ecological traits relate to this pattern remains requires broader taxonomic sampling and ecological data in future investigations.

research.abstract: Undernutrition is the leading risk factor for tuberculosis susceptibility, severity, and poor treatment outcome. Nutritional immunology and immunometabolism frame how nutrient availability and metabolism shape host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ) infection. By integrating targeted metabolomics and transcriptional profiling in a murine tuberculosis model, we defined immunometabolic programs underlying the transition from acute to chronic infection. Immune control of Mtb during acute infection was accompanied by robust activation of immune and metabolic programs, including mTORC1-associated signaling, glutaminolysis, glycolysis, arginine metabolism, and serine one-carbon metabolism, thereby highlighting the importance of amino acid metabolism and mitochondrial function in antimicrobial immunity. In contrast, chronic infection was characterized by reduced immune activation and mTORC1-associated signaling, increased branched-chain amino acid catabolism, and altered amino acid profiles, with leucine and glutamine among the discriminating metabolites. These findings suggest that reduced glutamine availability during chronic infection may increase reliance on leucine oxidative catabolism to sustain mitochondrial metabolism during nutrient stress, potentially limiting leucine availability for mTORC1-associated anabolic metabolism and immune activation. Oral glutamine supplementation restored amino acid homeostasis, including lung leucine abundance, enhanced mTORC1-associated signaling and central metabolic programs, moderately reduced bacterial burden and lung pathology, and mitigated infection-associated wasting. Reanalysis of published human metabolomics datasets further demonstrated reduced circulating glutamine levels during progression to active tuberculosis, supporting conservation of glutamine metabolic dysregulation across host species. Collectively, our findings identify a potential glutamine–leucine metabolic axis linking nutrient availability with immunometabolic competence and provide a mechanistic rationale for evaluating glutamine supplementation as a host-directed strategy for tuberculosis.

research.abstract: The GRAS gene family, a plant-specific family of transcription factors, plays critical roles in diverse developmental processes and abiotic stress responses. Although extensive studies on the identification and functional characterization of GRAS genes have been conducted in numerous plant species, systematic analyses of this family in Salvia miltiorrhiza, a valuable traditional Chinese medicinal herb, remain limited. The present study aims to identify and characterize GRAS genes in S. miltiorrhiza, thereby providing a comprehensive understanding of their phylogenetic evolution, functional divergence, and tissue-specific expression profiles​. In this study, a total of 33 GRAS genes were identified in S. miltiorrhiza and subjected to comprehensive analysis. Phylogenetic analysis classified these genes into eight distinct subgroups and identified eight pairs of paralogs. Genetic divergence analysis revealed that the GRAS gene family has predominantly undergone purifying selection, as evidenced by Ka/Ks ratios below 1 for all eight paralogous pairs. Positive selection analysis using the site and branch-site models further suggested that SmGRAS genes had gone through purifying selective pressure for adaptive evolution. Motif analysis showed that group-specific motifs likely contribute to functional divergence among subgroups. Functional divergence analysis suggested that subgroup-specific genes may have experienced functional divergence during evolution, and provided preliminary insights into the molecular mechanisms potentially underlying their divergent functions. Tissue-specific expression analysis revealed that SmGRAS genes might perform distinct functions in different tissues. This study presents a comprehensive characterization of the GRAS gene family in S. miltiorrhiza. Taken together, these results elucidate a comprehensive understanding of the GRAS gene family and furnish robust references for subsequent functional investigations of GRAS genes in S. miltiorrhiza.

research.abstract: Background Members of the Triatoma brasiliensis species complex are among the primary vectors of Chagas disease in northeastern Brazil. Despite their epidemiological importance, mitogenomic resources for this group remain limited, constraining comparative and evolutionary analyses at the genomic scale. Methods We assembled and annotated twelve near-complete mitochondrial genomes representing four taxa of the T. brasiliensis complex ( T. b. brasiliensis , T. melanica , T. sherlocki , and T. petrocchiae ), with three specimens per taxon. Genome annotation and gene-specific analyses were conducted to assess patterns of sequence and structural variation across taxa. A concatenated dataset including protein-coding genes, rRNAs, and tRNAs was analyzed under a partitioned maximum likelihood framework, with partitions defined by gene and codon position. Results All mitogenomes exhibited the canonical insect gene complement and gene order. Genome length variation (16,277–17,238 bp) involved variation in non-coding regions, including the A + T-rich control region and an expanded intergenic spacer between tRNA-Ser(UCN) and ND1 in T. petrocchiae, driven by tandem repeats. Among protein-coding genes, ND6 showed the highest nucleotide variability and elevated amino-acid variability relative to most other mitochondrial genes, with structural differences among the examined taxa. Phylogenetic analyses recovered the sampled members of the T. brasiliensis species complex as a fully supported monophyletic clade. Conclusion The marked variation observed in ND6, including distinct amino-acid motifs among the examined specimens, suggests that this gene may contain potentially informative variation for lineage-level evolutionary studies. However, the restricted geographic sampling, the limited number of specimens per taxon, and the incomplete representation of the T. brasiliensis complex constrain the generalizability of these findings. Broader geographic and taxonomic sampling will be required to determine the consistency and taxonomic significance of these patterns, while the mitogenomic dataset as a whole expands the resources available for investigating mitochondrial diversity and evolutionary relationships in Triatominae.

research.abstract: The convention that mutation is a random process has been challenged by suggestions that selection has acted on between-gene variation in the mutation rate, with claims that more important genes are protected from mutation in part, in prokaryotes, by being on the leading strand, while those required for rapid adaptive evolution have higher mutation rates, in part by being on the lagging strand. The original selectionist claims have proven contentious with several replication failures. However, none of the replication attempts fully allow for covariates and many employ data from mismatch repair (MMR) knockout strains. To address these limitations, we consider amassed mutation accumulation data for wild-type Escherichia coli , the focal species for adaptive claims, and Saccharomyces cerevisiae , in a multiple parameter-controlled analysis to predict between-gene variation in mutational density (mutations per base pair). Along with covariates, we consider putative selectively relevant parameters: protein level and essentiality to capture genic “importance”, and, in E. coli , strand with respect to DNA replication. We consider deviation of correlation and partial correlation values from those expected under trinucleotide-controlled simulations. While in E. coli more highly transcribed genes may have slightly lower mutation rates, potentially consistent with a selectionist model, the same is not seen in yeast, and in neither species do genes for more abundant or essential proteins have lower mutation rates. In E. coli there is no difference in mutation rate between genes on different strands, a lack of difference replicated in other prokaryotes. The degree of purifying selection is also not predictive of mutation density. We additionally highlight a strong artefact seen using the standard off-the-shelf statistical approach and note that results from MMR-deficient strains are discordant. We conclude that as trends are nearly uniformly unsupportive, not consistent between species and of miniscule effect size, they present no challenge to convention.

research.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Sputum culture conversion in patients with pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) is the most important interim indicator for drug-resistant (DR) tuberculosis (TB) treatment effectiveness. Bedaquiline-based regimens offer the possibility of more effective and less toxic treatment for DR TB. Bedaquiline-based regimens have been adopted as the new standard of care for DR TB, replacing the oto-and nephrotoxic aminoglycosides. We determined the median time to sputum culture conversion (TTCC) and associated factors among RR and MDR TB patients treated with Bedaquiline-based regimens, at Mulago National Referral Hospital, Uganda. METHODS: In a longitudinal type of observational study performed at Mulago Hospital, between January 2020 and June 2023, RR and MDR TB patients' records were reviewed to obtain data on socio-demographic and clinical factors, and TTCC. The study outcome was TTCC, recorded as time from RR/MDR TB treatment initiation to sputum culture conversion, which was defined as at least 2 consecutive negative TB sputum cultures, at least 30 days apart, for a RR/MDR PTB patient who was sputum culture positive at baseline. Analysis for median TTCC was done using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and the log-logistic parametric survival regression model was used to identify predictors for TTCC. RESULTS: Of the 265 participants, 196 (74.0%) were male, with median age of 35(IQR:27-42) years. The median TTCC was 7 (IQR:4-8) weeks from treatment initiation. Grade 2 + baseline smear positivity (adjusted Time Ratio (aTR):1.24, 95% CI:1.02-1.51, p = 0.029), grade 3 + baseline smear positivity (aTR:1.62, 95% CI:1.30-2.01, p < 0.001), cavitary disease on CXR (aTR:1.36, 95% CI:1.18-1.56, p < 0.001), and pleural effusion on CXR (aTR:1.81, 95% CI:1.43-2.31, p < 0.001) significantly prolonged the TTCC. Diabetes mellitus (7/265) significantly reduced the TTCC (aTR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.22 - 0.60, p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The WHO long regimen (9 months) was indistinguishable from the shorter 6-months regimen for the time to culture conversion. Integration of TB screening at points of care of high-risk patients like diabetics remains important for early detection and prompt initiation of DR TB treatment for better outcomes. The TB program and clinicians should enhance and individualize support for RR/MDR TB patients with more severe disease, to ensure optimum TTCC and successful treatment outcomes. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: India, the capital of tuberculosis (TB) worldwide, accounts for 27% of the global burden of drug-resistant TB (DR-TB). Managing DR-TB in itself is challenging, and preexisting multiorgan dysfunction makes it even more lengthy and complex. Here, we share our real-world experience in successfully managing a difficult-to-treat case of rifampicin-resistant TB (RR-TB), a type of DR-TB, in a high-risk patient with multiple comorbidities. CASE PRESENTATION: A 60-year-old 70 kg male diagnosed with RR-TB was referred from a District DR-TB Centre to our Nodal DR-TB Centre for pretreatment evaluation and treatment initiation in December 2022. Baseline evaluation revealed severe renal dysfunction, hepatic dysfunction, a prolonged QT interval, and poorly controlled diabetes mellitus, necessitating an individualized all-oral longer regimen with appropriate dose adjustments guided by the National Programmatic Management of Drug-resistant Tuberculosis Guidelines. During treatment, the regimen was sequentially individualized in response to evolving suspected adverse drug reactions, with each modification aimed at optimizing patient safety while maintaining an effective treatment regimen. The patient showed radiological improvement, achieved sputum culture conversion, and successfully completed the 18-month treatment by June 2024. The patient did not relapse during the 18-month follow-up period (December 2025). CONCLUSION: This case report exemplifies the success of personalized pharmacotherapeutic decision-making in challenging cases. Structured toxicity assessment and intensive clinical, laboratory, and electrocardiography monitoring in addition to timely treatment modification may facilitate successful treatment in carefully selected high-risk RR-TB patients when standard regimens are not feasible, even in resource-limited settings. research.abstract: Objectives: This study compared a convolutional neural network (CNN) and linear regression for predicting mean hearing thresholds at the last audiogram and their variation from the first audiogram. It used audiometric and clinical data from older adults with bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Markov chains estimated hearing- loss worsening and stability probabilities between assessments. Analyses considered hypertension, diabetes, occupational noise exposure and age. Design: This retrospective study analysed serial audiograms and clinical records. Data included 823 adults with bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Predictive analyses included 394 complete-case records, with 79 records per ear in the independent test set. Cross- validation selected model configurations and evaluated predictive performance across data partitions. Markov chains estimated worsening and stability probabilities across hearing-loss severity categories. Results: CNN achieved cross-validation mean absolute errors of 6.475 dB HL (right ear, RE) and 6.047 dB HL (left ear, LE) and linear regression registered 6.054 dB HL (RE) and 6.170 dB HL (LE). CNN (independent evaluation) showed significantly lower prediction error in the LE after Holm correction (padj = 0.0328). No significant advantage was observed in the RE (padj = 0.1969). Markov state-averaged conditional worsening probabilities were 34.0% (RE) and 35.3% (LE). Observed worsening proportions were 42.2% (RE; 347/823) and 40.9% (LE; 337/823). Corresponding stability probabilities were 57.8% (RE) and 58.6% (LE). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed for occupational noise exposure, hypertension, or diabetes. Worsening estimates increased across age groups. Conclusions: This study provides conditional probabilities of hearing-loss worsening and stability in older adults. CNN predictions and Markov estimates suggest that threshold prediction and severity transitions offer complementary descriptions of hearing changes. The ear-specific CNN advantage warrants further investigation. This characterisation may support assessment of changes in hearing thresholds alongside progression to more severe hearing-loss categories.

research.abstract: Abstract Myxococcota are globally distributed bacteria renowned for their remarkable ecological and biotechnological significance due to their complex lifestyles, social behaviour, and secondary metabolite production. Despite their ubiquity in diverse environments, including soil, marine, and extreme habitats, their diversity and ecological roles remain underexplored. Here, we used the Microflora Danica dataset, encompassing >10,000 metagenomes and >400 rRNA gene datasets from various environments in Denmark, to investigate the distribution, diversity, and metabolic potential of Myxococcota. We show that Myxococcota are ubiquitous but their distribution is structured by environment, with soil-associated lineages enriched in predatory and multicellular development traits, whereas aquatic-associated taxa, particularly those from anoxic sediments, exhibit a higher potential of anaerobic metabolism and phototrophy. Comparative genomic analysis reveals widespread metabolic potential for secondary metabolite production, hydrocarbon degradation, and organohalide transformation, alongside predicted diverse contribution to carbon and nutrient cycling. Together, these findings propose Myxococcota as a functionally diverse and ecologically differentiated phylum, extending beyond canonical predation and multicellularity, and shows their promise as a reservoir of unexplored functional potential for biotechnological applications in drug discovery and environmental remediation.

research.abstract: Abstract The Wnt gene family plays a central role in vertebrate development, yet its evolutionary dynamics across lineages remain largely unexplored. Here, we present the most comprehensive analysis of Wnt gene evolution in vertebrates to date, leveraging a large-scale comparative genomics approach of 38,886 Wnt gene sequences mined from 1,961 species. We first investigate overall patterns of gene retention, duplication, and loss, and then focus specifically on the impact of whole-genome duplications (WGDs). We uncover striking variation in Wnt gene repertoire sizes, with ray-finned fishes (Actinopterygii) exhibiting the largest repertoires – even after excluding taxa with recent WGDs. Notably, we identify extreme expansions in polyploid cyprinids, including an octoploid hybrid harbouring 99 Wnt genes, the highest number observed. Unexpectedly elevated Wnt copy numbers in diploid species, such as in the Antarctic lanternfish (Electrona antarctica) and the brook lamprey (Lethenteron reissneri), point to lineage-specific expansions, although the potential adaptive significance of these expansions remains to be tested. Evolutionary rate analyses reveal that certain Wnt clades – especially Wnt8 and Wnt16 – exhibit elevated dN/dS ratios and high birth–death rates, consistent with repeated episodes of relaxed constraint and/or adaptive diversification. Contrary to our expectations, there was no relationship between developmental expression timing and evolutionary rates, suggesting pleiotropic regulation and functional redundancy of Wnt genes. Altogether, our findings reveal widespread variation in Wnt copy number and turnover among lineages, shaped by both genome duplication history and divergent evolutionary trajectories. This work provides a high-resolution framework for understanding the molecular evolution of a key developmental toolkit and highlights candidate genes for future studies of vertebrate eco-morphological diversity.

research.abstract: Background: Takotsubo syndrome, which predominantly affects women, is thought to be precipitated by catecholamine excess, yet unstable patients often receive intravenous inotropes. We examined the association between intravenous inotropes and 30-day mortality in a nationwide cohort. Methods: We identified all patients with a first angiographic diagnosis of Takotsubo syndrome in the Swedish Coronary Angiography and Angioplasty Registry from 2008 through August 2025, linked to coronary care and population registers. The primary analysis was a Cox model for 30-day death among patients with a coronary care record, adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, smoking, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and Killip class, with multiple imputation. Sensitivity analyses varied the covariates and standard errors and examined days 0 to 7 and 8 to 30 separately, and the association was estimated in women and men with an interaction term. Results: Of 3,458 patients (79.4% women), 141 (4.1%) received inotropes: 3.6% of women and 5.8% of men. Thirty-day mortality was 19.9% in treated and 1.7% in untreated patients. The unadjusted hazard ratio was 12.89 (95% CI, 8.20 to 20.26) and the adjusted hazard ratio 6.49 (3.49 to 12.08; P<0.001; E-value, 12.5). In sensitivity analyses, the hazard ratio ranged from 3.37 (1.88 to 6.03), with presenting symptom and laboratory values added, to 6.62 (3.63 to 12.08). The hazard ratio was 8.82 (4.47 to 17.39) for days 0 to 7 and 2.47 (0.65 to 9.36) for days 8 to 30, and 6.43 (3.15 to 13.16) in women and 6.59 (2.79 to 15.58) in men (P=0.96 for interaction). Conclusions: Intravenous inotropes were associated with higher 30-day mortality in Takotsubo syndrome, in both women and men, with most of the excess in the first week.

research.abstract: INTRODUCTION: TB (tuberculosis) due to Mycobacterium tuberculosis continues to be a significant worldwide health issue. Timely and reliable diagnostic tests will improve treatment outcomes and reduce the spread of disease. Traditional TB diagnostics currently available, such as smear microscopy and culture, have significant limitations with regard to sensitivity and turnaround times, especially for smear-negative cases and for tuberculosis in extrapulmonary locations. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this review is to analyze the evolution of TB diagnostics from traditional microbiology to new molecular diagnostic methods (including CRISPR, biosensor technology, and microfluidic methods), including an assessment of their diagnostic testing performance, feasibility, and potential for the future. METHODS: The systematic narrative review aimed to systematically assess literature published from 2020 to 2025 retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. The review was carried out according to the PRISMA guidelines and included 89 studies after screening and assessing for eligibility. The data were analysed qualitatively (i.e., through thematic analysis) by comparing data from conventional, molecular, and next-generation diagnostic methods. RESULTS: Molecular tests (e.g., GeneXpert, Line Probe Assays, PCR, and Whole Genome Sequencing) provide greater sensitivity and specificity than traditional methods and allow for faster diagnosis. Additionally, newer CRISPR-based tests, biosensors, and microfluidic devices hold promise for rapid, portable, point-of-care diagnosis of tuberculosis. DISCUSSION: The findings indicate that molecular diagnostics improve rapid detection and drug-resistance profiling, while CRISPR and biosensor platforms offer potential for rapid point-of-care testing. However, affordability, infrastructure, clinical validation, and scalability remain important barriers. CONCLUSION: The use of molecular diagnostic testing, CRISPR technology, biosensors, artificial intelligence, and portable platforms will dramatically enhance existing TB surveillance systems and strategies for controlling the disease globally.

research.abstract: Abstract Diabetes is a known risk factor for tuberculosis (TB), but clinical evidences suggest that TB itself can induce hyperglycaemia and insulin resistance, though the underlying mycobacterial factors are not known. Herein, we implicate PPE2, a secretory PE/PPE family protein of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), as a key modulator of adipose tissue physiology that contributes to the development of insulin resistance. In mice, PPE2 caused fat loss, adipocyte hypertrophy, immune cell infiltration, impaired glucose tolerance, reduced expression of PPAR-γ, C/EBP-α, adiponectin and higher insulin resistance. Transcriptomic analysis revealed PPE2 altered expression of genes associated with chemokine/cytokine, ribosomal biogenesis and lipase signaling. PPE2 induced lipolysis by activating cAMP-PKA-HSL axis, increased circulating free fatty acids, a feature also observed in TB patient sera. Interestingly, PPE2-immunization mitigated these effects, suggesting its potential as a subunit vaccine. Overall, this study identifies PPE2 as a key link between Mtb-infection, adipose tissue dysfunction and insulin resistance.

research.abstract: Background Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a common complication of diabetes, and in Bangladesh laboratory testing for it is not always available. Questionnaire answers could help decide whom to test first, but small machine-learning studies often report optimistic accuracy. Methods We analysed a public dataset of 400 adults with at least 10 years of diabetes attending a tertiary hospital in Dhaka, 185 with a hospital diagnosis of CKD. A pre-specified ridge logistic regression using 20 non-invasive features was developed and internally validated with nested cross-validation (five folds, ten repeats), compared with lasso, random forest and gradient boosting, and assessed for discrimination, calibration and net benefit. Simulations examined case-enriched sampling and single train/test splits. Results The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.75 (95% confidence interval 0.70-0.80; optimism-corrected 0.76). Flexible algorithms were not detectably better (differences -0.005 to +0.006). Calibration within the sample was good (slope 1.06, 0.79-1.33), and testing the highest-scoring 30% of patients would have found 48% of CKD cases. The sample was smaller than the 883 patients recommended. Urinary infection, body-mass index, insulin use, diabetes duration and pain-killer use were positively associated with CKD and diet adherence negatively; regular walking and hypertension showed directions opposite to clinical expectation, consistent with features recorded after diagnosis. The yearly history added no reliable information. In simulation, case-enriched sampling preserved the AUC but overstated absolute risk (mean predicted risk 0.37 at a true prevalence of 0.10). Over 300 random 80/20 splits of the same data, the test AUC ranged from 0.61 to 0.87; reporting the best of ten splits would overstate it by about 0.07. Conclusions Questionnaire features moderately distinguished patients with an existing CKD diagnosis. Whether they identify patients before diagnosis requires external validation in patients assessed before CKD status is known. The study was not registered.

research.abstract: Background Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors reduce cardiovascular and kidney events in adults with type 2 diabetes(T2DM) and cardiorenal disease, but treatment initiation among eligible patients remains incompletely characterized. We estimated the cumulative incidence of recorded SGLT2 inhibitor initiation and associated participant characteristics in a diverse U.S. cohort. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study leveraging electronic health record data from the All of Us Research Program. Adults with confirmed type 2 diabetes, at least one co-occurring cardiorenal condition (atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease), and no prior SGLT2 inhibitor use were followed from the earliest date all criteria were met during 2019-2023. The 365-day cumulative incidence of initiation was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method, accounting for competing risk of all-cause mortality. Cause-specific modified Poisson regression with robust error variance yielded adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for initiation predictors Results Among 9,333 eligible participants, 637 had recorded SGLT2 inhibitor initiation within 365 days (estimated cumulative incidence, 6.85% (95% CI 6.34-7.36)). The 365-day incidence was 8.40% among individuals with heart failure, 6.65% with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and 5.28% with chronic kidney disease. Initiation was more likely with heart failure (RR 1.51, 95% CI 1.29-1.76), and glycated hemoglobin [≥]9.0% versus <7.0% (RR 2.61, 95% CI 2.07-3.28), but less likely with chronic kidney disease (RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.54-0.74), age [≥]75 versus 45-64 years (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.40-0.65), and non-Hispanic Black versus non-Hispanic White race and ethnicity (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.65-0.97). Conclusions Fewer than 1 in 10 eligible, untreated adults with T2D and cardiorenal disease initiated SGLT2 inhibitor therapy within one year. Even with expanding guideline indications, substantial implementation gaps persist, particularly among patients with CKD, older adults, and non-Hispanic Black adults. Targeted health systems are imperative to optimize the use of guideline-recommended cardiorenal therapies.

research.abstract: Computing phylogenetic likelihoods becomes challenging when the continuous-time Markov chain has a large state space. At each branch, pruning algorithms require terms of the form $e^{Q t}\cdot B$, where $Q$ is an $S \times S$ rate matrix (e.g., for $S$ states), $t$ is a branch length, and the columns of matrix $B$ (e.g., $B \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{S \times L}$) are partial-likelihood vectors for $L$ site patterns. Many implementations calculate the dense transition matrix $P(t)=e^{Q t}$ via eigendecomposition and multiply it by $B$. This strategy is efficient for small state spaces, but it can be inefficient for large sparse rate matrices because forming $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices destroys sparsity and its cost may not be well amortized when $L$ is small. We implement an alternative likelihood kernel based on the Al-Mohy and Higham (2011) algorithm for computing the action of the matrix exponential directly, avoiding explicit construction of $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices. The resulting method takes full advantage of the sparsity of $Q$. We implement this method as a CPU-based extension to the BEAGLE library and evaluate it on two large-state molecular models: a Markov-modulated codon model of heterotachy with $M$ selective regimes and $61\cdot M$ possible states, and a codon-pair model of interlocus gene conversion between two paralogs with $61^2=3\,721$ possible states. Our results characterize when action-based likelihood computation improves performance over calculating $e^{Q t}$ directly. We show that this method enables fast, scalable inference for complex models, removing a key computational barrier to the study of evolution with large state space models.

research.abstract: Despite transformative advances in continuous glucose monitoring, current continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) still relies on transcutaneous needle-based sensors that measure glucose in the interstitial fluid, which lags behind blood glucose. Mid-infrared optoacoustic sensing (MiROS) has recently demonstrated a sensitivity to glucose changes of a few tens of mg/dL in mice using non-invasive measurements. However, the relation of MiROS to human measurements remains unknown. We conducted a MiROS pilot study in 30 healthy participants undergoing oral glucose tolerance tests and investigated how optoacoustic signals reflect tissue optical-property variations associated with changes in blood glucose concentration. We defined the Optoacoustic Mid-infrared Signal (OMS) as a readout of glucose-induced alterations in tissue optical properties and compared it with reference blood glucose measurements. The OMS corresponded to a mean absolute error (MAE) of 11.9 mg/dL and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 10% relative to the reference blood analysis. More than 99.9% of paired OMS values were located in zones A and B of the consensus error grid. The study further showed that OMS compared favourably with concurrently acquired CGM measurements, which showed an MAE of 15.7 mg/dL and a MAPE of 12% and exhibited an average time lag of 10.5 min relative to blood glucose. No comparable lag was observed for the OMS. These results support MiROS as a promising framework pointing to a sensor with potential for non-invasive glucose sensing in humans, in the future, and a potential step toward less burdensome glucose monitoring for diabetes management.

research.abstract: H14 avian influenza viruses (AIVs) are rare, with limited data on their circulation in mainland China. This study investigated the ecological origins and zoonotic potential of H14 viruses in southern China. The isolates were characterised by full-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis, together with assessment of avian- and human-type receptor binding, in vitro replication in avian, mammalian, and human cell lines, and in vivo pathogenicity in mice. Four H14 AIVs (one H14N6, two H14N7, and one H14N8) were isolated. We identified a novel H14 transmission network involving Mareca penelope and various shorebird species, indicating a multihost dispersal mechanism. Guangdong isolates formed a distinct subclade within the Eurasian lineage, closely related to Russian and Cambodian strains. The isolates (SZ3742/H14N6, ZJ3523/H14N7, SZ3536/H14N8) exhibited dual receptor-binding specificity for avian (α-2,3) and human (α-2,6) sialic acids. Strain-dependent replication in human A549 cells showed SZ3742/H14N6 peaked comparably to DF-1 cells but lower than MDCK cells, while the others had lower peak titres. All isolates replicated transiently at low titres in mouse lungs with limited pathogenicity. Molecular characterisation revealed mammalian adaptation markers and a typical HA cleavage site motif (PDKQTR↓GLF). This study presents the first evidence of H14 AIV circulation in Guangdong, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance in the East Asian -Australasian Flyway.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is an increasingly prevalent neurodevelopmental condition with multifactorial origins, including potential prenatal environmental contributions. Maternal anemia (decreased hemoglobin [Hb] levels) has long been associated with adverse offspring neurodevelopmental outcomes, yet evidence regarding elevated levels of antenatal hemoglobin levels, in relation to ASD risk remains limited. This study evaluated the association between maternal Hb levels during pregnancy and the risk of ASD diagnosis in offspring. Methods This large-scale, population-based retrospective cohort study used electronic health records from births of members of Clalit Health Services (CHS), the largest health maintenance organization in Israel, between 2011 and 2021. The study included 303,234 singleton live births to Jewish mothers who had at least one measured prenatal Hb value and were CHS members. Exclusion criteria were children with known genetic disorders and births <25 weeks of gestation. Maternal Hb, and red blood cells (RBC) levels during the first and second trimesters were categorized as low (<2.5th percentile), normal (reference), or high (>97.5th percentile). The main outcome was a diagnosis of ASD in the offspring, as recorded in medical files. Statistical analyses adjusted for maternal age, socioeconomic status, gestational diabetes, BMI, and other clinical and demographic factors. Results Among the 303,234 births, 8,106 (2.7%) children were diagnosed with ASD. High maternal Hb levels were associated with elevated odds of ASD diagnosis (aOR=1.22; 95% CI=1.08-1.37), with the strongest association observed for first-trimester measurements (aOR=1.31; 95% CI=1.14-1.49). This association persisted in the sibling-matched analysis (aOR=1.64; 95% CI=1.08–2.47) and was not modified by maternal RBC levels, suggesting that it was not explained by familial factors or RBC counts. The main limitations of this study include the lack of available data on maternal smoking, and the absence of detailed information on maternal nutritional status. Conclusions These findings suggest that elevated antenatal Hb levels may be relevant to offspring neurodevelopment. Further studies are needed to replicate these findings and clarify the biological mechanisms underlying this association.

research.abstract: Comparative genomics often turns a trait into a hypothesis about selection by labelling the branches that carry it and testing them against the rest. We asked how such a test behaves when the labels carry no trait. In three panels of about 50 species, fungi, yeasts and lactobacilli, two of them registered in advance, randomly placed terminal labels on presumed-null single-copy genes were rejected by PAML's two-ratio branch model in 65.9, 68.8 and 88.8% of genes, against a nominal 5%. Referring each real gene to replicates simulated under its own fitted null model did not remove the excess: with a generator matched to the depth of the real alignments, 65.0% (95% CI 53.5-75.3) and 83.8% (73.8-91.1) of 80 genes were still rejected. On the same genes the branch-site test, which asks only for positive selection on the labelled branches, rejected none after refitting, though on alignments simulated from its own fitted model it detected positive selection placed on all those branches in 95-100% of replicates, and replicates simulated under each gene's fitted per-branch {omega} rejected 1 of 40 genes against 28 of 40 for a control carrying only the noise of that fit: {omega} plausibly varies among branches on real genes, so that a randomly chosen set of branches does differ from the rest, though the fitted pattern is an upper bound. Under correct specification at the depth of the data the same test rejected random terminal labels in 5.4 and 6.8% of replicates, and internal labels of matched summed length differed from them by +0.2 and -1.2 percentage points. On earlier simulations from a site-mixture model, moving the labels from terminal to internal branches raised the rejection rate 1.3-fold on genes with a moderate fitted {omega} and 6.2-fold where a fitted class reached {omega} [≥] 100, in interaction with the fitted model. A trait label should therefore be read against random labels of the same size rather than against {chi}^2, and a reference simulated from the fitted model is not enough. The count question asked of the fungal panel is answerable: the within-genome ratio of plant-cell-wall-degrading enzymes to other carbohydrate-active enzymes is 0.473 times as large in ectomycorrhizal genomes as in free-living decomposers.

research.abstract: Phylogenetic network inference methods are increasingly used to detect hybridization and gene [fl]ow from genomic data, but their robustness to common sources of model violation remains poorly characterized. We conducted a simulation study to evaluate the e[ff]ects of hidden paralogy and substitution rate variation on three commonly used network inference methods: find_graphs from ADMIXTOOLS 2, SNaQ and PhyNEST. Using eight-taxon species trees calibrated from empirical reptile and plant phylogenies, we simulated data under various levels of hidden paralogy (from none to strong) and three levels of rate variation (none, gene-speci[fi]c, and lineage-speci[fi]c). We found that hidden paralogy had limited impact on network inference under the conditions examined. In contrast, lineage-speci[fi]c rates severely biased find_graphs, in[fl]ating worst f -statistic residuals well beyond the standard acceptance threshold. Under lineage-speci[fi]c rates, PhyNEST had high type I error rates and was less likely to recover the true species topologies. SNaQ mostly selected the correct tree model, even under lineage-speci[fi]c rates. Its networks inferred generally displayed the true tree, although recovery of the reptile tree declined under lineage-speci[fi]c rates. We also show that the standard worst residuals threshold of 3 for find_graphs produces in[fl]ated type I error even without rate variation, as did the calibrated thresholds for PhyNEST, which di[ff]ered between species trees and ILS levels. We therefore recommend empirical calibration of the model-selection threshold within each study system, and recommend caution using find_graphs and PhyNEST when rate variation across lineages is suspected.
