research.abstract: ABSTRACT RfaH, a member of the universally conserved NusG/Spt5 family, activates transcription and translation of virulence genes by bridging the transcribing RNA polymerase to the translating ribosome. Unlike its monomorphic, constitutively active paralog NusG, RfaH fold-switches from an autoinhibited state, wherein its C-terminal domain forms an α-helical hairpin bound to the N-terminal domain, into an active NusG-like state through C-terminal domain dissociation and refolding into a β-barrel. RfaH has been proposed to evolve from NusG via gene duplication by first activating genes adjacent to its production site, before developing autoinhibition to selectively control distant genes. Using AlphaFold2, we predicted the structures of thousands of RfaH homologs and identified a subset (∼14%) that appear predominantly folded in the active state. In vivo assays confirmed that these putative monomorphic homologs exhibit constitutive activity comparable to known RfaH mutants. Phylogenetic and genomic analyses revealed that these monomorphic proteins form a distinct clade and are preferentially located within or next to long virulence-associated operons. Together, these results further support a stepwise evolutionary model of RfaH specialization through structural transformation.

research.abstract: Abstract Background The HSP70 family maintains cellular proteostasis and mediates vertebrate responses to environmental stress. The Chinese alligator ( Alligator sinensis ), an ectothermic crocodilian, undergoes winter dormancy characterized by cessation of feeding, reduced activity, and metabolic depression. However, the evolutionary patterns of the HSP70 family across vertebrates and their potential relevance to winter dormancy in crocodilians remain poorly understood. We characterized the HSP70 family across 24 vertebrate species, focusing on the molecular evolution of HSPA12A along crocodilian lineages and its seasonal expression in the hypothalamus of the Chinese alligator. Results Using HMMER- and BLAST-based searches, we identified 355 HSP70 family members, with 11–28 members per species. Phylogenetic, synteny, and subcellular localization analyses indicated that the family is broadly conserved but exhibits subfamily- and lineage-associated divergence. Under two foreground schemes in which the terminal branches of two winter-dormant crocodilians or all four crocodilian species were jointly designated as foreground, HSPA12A showed an elevated relative evolutionary rate and significant evidence of positive selection. HyPhy aBSREL supported episodic diversifying selection on the A. sinensis HSPA12A terminal branch. Public RNA-seq data showed that HSPA12A expression was highest in the hypothalamus among sampled female tissues and was higher in winter than in summer (600.0 and 329.2 TPM, respectively). Western blotting and immunofluorescence analyses showed descriptive differences between the examined specimens, with higher HSPA12A protein abundance and a higher density of cells double-positive for anti-HSPA12A antibody immunoreactivity and NeuN in winter. Because each RNA-seq, western blotting, and immunofluorescence comparison included only one biological specimen per season, these observations were treated as descriptive, and no inferential statistical comparisons were performed. Conclusions The vertebrate HSP70 family is broadly conserved but shows differentiation among subfamilies and lineages. The evolutionary analyses indicate a broader crocodilian-lineage-associated pattern of HSPA12A evolution that cannot be attributed specifically to winter dormancy. Separately, the descriptive transcriptomic and preliminary protein-level observations provide a basis for considering HSPA12A as a candidate for further investigation in relation to winter physiology in the Chinese alligator. These findings do not establish winter dormancy as the selective driver of HSPA12A evolution, and its biological function and causal role remain to be determined.

research.abstract: Camelids have evolved remarkable physiological adaptations enabling survival in extreme desert environments, yet the genomic basis of these traits remains incompletely understood. We conducted a comparative genomic analysis across eleven mammalian species, including three Old World camels, four New World camels, two additional artiodactyls (pig, cattle), and two outgroups (human, mouse), to identify lineage-specific molecular signatures of adaptation. Using OrthoFinder, we constructed orthologous gene families and identified 11,861 single-copy orthologs across all species. We detected significant copy-number changes in cytochrome P450 gene families, with expansion of CYP2J and contraction of CYP4F in the camelid ancestor, suggesting a shift toward anti-inflammatory eicosanoid signaling. Branch-site analyses identified 47 high-confidence positively selected genes in Old World camels, including HACD3, a fatty acid elongation enzyme harboring an ultraconserved substitution (D270N). Structural modeling and conservation analysis suggest that this substitution may hypothetically alter protein conformation, but this prediction awaits experimental validation. Tissue-specific RNA-seq analysis confirmed that HACD3 is expressed in camel kidney and liver, tissues central to lipid metabolism and water conservation. Systematic screening for inactivating mutations identified ten high-confidence pseudogenized genes, including CES3, CPA3, and PLA2G2F, enriched in lipid metabolism and epidermal pathways. The adaptive significance of these losses is currently hypothetical and inferred from homologous gene studies in mice and humans; because some of the cited genes are paralogs rather than orthologs, and because mouse and human phenotypes may not transfer to camels, these inferences are hypothesis-generating only and do not establish camel gene function. Experimental validation confirmed pseudogenization of TAS2R16, and cell-based calcium-signalling assays showed that the camel receptor fails to respond to salicin. This establishes loss of receptor function but not its adaptive significance; both dietary-breadth and neutral (relaxed-selection or drift) explanations remain compatible with the data. For CES3, CPA3, and PLA2G2F, functional consequences in camels remain unverified and require camel-specific experimental validation. Collectively, these results provide a comprehensive framework of gene family evolution, positive selection, and gene loss underlying desert adaptation in camelids, while highlighting that expression patterns are correlative only and do not demonstrate that the identified variants alter protein function or physiology.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Dosing guidance for children with leprosy remains operationally challenging. For children under 10 years of age, current WHO recommendations rely on mg/kg dosing of the three separate components of leprosy multidrug therapy, which are difficult to implement in routine care and may result in inconsistent drug exposures. Weight-banded dosing offers a pragmatic alternative that better aligns with pharmacokinetic principles and existing drug formulations. Methodology A pharmacokinetic simulation study was conducted to develop harmonized weight-banded dosing regimens for rifampicin, clofazimine, and dapsone in children aged 2 to 10 years. Using the WHO dosing tool, drug exposures across harmonized weight bands were simulated and adult-equivalent systemic exposure (80–125% of adult area under the concentration–time curve) targeted. Predicted exposures were contextualized against safety reference regimens used in tuberculosis meningitis, multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, and leprosy. An iterative review process involving the WHO Technical Working Group on leprosy in children ensured clinical and operational feasibility. Results Proposed weight-banded multidrug therapy regimens achieved adult-equivalent exposures across most weight bands. Predicted exposures modestly exceeded 125% of adult levels at the lower end of selected weight bands but remained well below safety benchmarks, namely exposures associated with daily rifampicin therapy for tuberculosis meningitis and clofazimine regimens for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. Dapsone exposures were comparable to those achieved with current leprosy dosing. The existing 10–14-year-old child MDT blister pack could be used without modification in children weighing 25–39.9 kg and with limited tablet or gel capsule removal in children weighing 6–24.9 kg. Conclusions A harmonized weight-banded dosing strategy was developed that enables effective, practical dosing of leprosy multidrug therapy in children under 10 years using existing free-of-charge blister packs provided through WHO. This approach improves dosing consistency, supports programmatic implementation, and provides a rational interim solution while child-friendly formulations are being developed. Author Summary Leprosy continues to affect children in many low-resource settings, yet guidance on how to dose treatment in younger children remains limited. Current recommendations often require clinicians to calculate mg/kg doses, which can be difficult in practice and may not match the oral formulations that are available. In this study, we used computer-based simulations to develop a simplified dosing approach for the three drugs used to treat leprosy. We showed that grouping children into weight bands, rather than calculating individual doses, can achieve drug exposures similar to those seen in adults, where treatment is known to be effective. Importantly, we found that these doses can be delivered using existing pre-packed treatment kits by removing selected dose units, making this approach practical in routine care. This work provides a more straightforward and reliable way to treat children with leprosy, reducing the burden on clinicians and improving access to treatment. However, challenges remain, including the lack of child-friendly formulations and limited data on how these drugs behave in children. Further studies are needed to improve treatment for this vulnerable population.

research.abstract: IntroductionAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) to first line antibiotics for pneumonia is a major global health problem, and AMR-attributable deaths are prevalent in sub-Saharan Africa. Improved data on how AMR develops and influences health outcomes in resource limited settings is crucial. The nasopharynx is a reservoir for pneumonia pathogens and their resistome, the genetic determinants of AMR. No study has explored whether human resistome composition in children with pneumonia is associated with health outcomes. This study will examine whether antibiotic treatment and hospital admission for pneumonia generate a persistent hospital-acquired nasopharyngeal resistome in children, and whether this is associated with re-hospitalisation. MethodsThis is an observational case-control study, that will recruit 350 children aged 12-36 months from four groups in Blantyre, Malawi: healthy children in the community (healthy community), children with pneumonia treated in the community (community pneumonia), children hospitalised with pneumonia (hospital pneumonia) and children re-hospitalised with pneumonia (re-hospitalised pneumonia). Nasopharyngeal swabs will be taken at recruitment and 3-month follow-up study visits for metagenomic sequencing to characterise the nasopharyngeal microbiome and resistome; urine samples will be taken at recruitment for an antibiotic activity bioassay. Socio-demographic data, co-morbidities, pneumonia severity, antibiotic exposure and health outcomes will be recorded. AnalysisCross-sectional comparisons between groups at recruitment will examine whether nasopharyngeal resistome (NPR) composition differs by pneumonia severity, antibiotic and healthcare exposure. Longitudinal comparisons within groups will assess the dynamics of NPR composition over time. The study is powered to detect a medium effect size (Cohens D = 0.505) change in the relative abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) between all four groups. Primary outcomes are the difference in beta diversity (Bray-Curtis dissimilarity index), and relative abundance of ARG classes in the NPR. The primary objectives are to estimate the difference in diversity and relative abundance of the NPR between hospitalised pneumonia participants when compared to 1) healthy community and 2) community pneumonia participants, and to investigate whether participants re-hospitalised with pneumonia within a 3-month period have a persistent hospital-acquired NPR pattern. Ethics and disseminationThe study has been approved by the Kamuzu University of Heath Sciences Research Ethics Committee (KUREC, formerly Malawi College of Medicine Research Ethics Committee; Ref: P.10/24-1200) and Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine Research Ethics Committee (LSTM REC; Ref: 24-076). C_LIO_LIData on reported and urinary bioassay-detected antibiotic use prior to, and throughout the study, enabling detailed examination of antibiotic selective pressure on the NPR. C_LIO_LIInvestigation of the association between NPR composition and adverse clinical outcomes from pneumonia. C_LI LimitationsO_LILimitations to this study include few sampling time points (two for community pneumonia and three for hospitalised pneumonia), which may not fully capture the impact of antibiotic exposure; the potential for residual confounding following adjustment for known potential confounders (e.g. age, sex, co-morbidities, household exposure to smoke and breastfeeding) in the association between resistome composition and adverse clinical outcomes, for which the authors have detailed statistical analysis measures; and ability to only determine association between NPR composition and adverse clinical outcomes, rather than causal inference, due to the case-control study design. C_LI SUMMARYO_ST_ABSWhat is already known on this topicC_ST_ABSThe nasopharynx is a reservoir for pneumonia pathogens and their genetic determinants of antibiotic resistance in children. Studies of nasopharyngeal microbiome composition have shown association with paediatric pneumonia severity and mortality. What this study addsThis study will describe nasopharyngeal resistome (NPR) evolution under selective pressure of antibiotics and hospitalisation for paediatric pneumonia, and explore whether NPR composition is associated with health outcomes in a resource-limited setting. How this study might affect research, practice or policyThis exploratory study could inform larger scale observational studies to examine the association between antibiotic resistance and health outcomes, by defining high-risk nasopharyngeal resistome composition, helping to determine the required sample size and contributing open-source bioinformatic pipelines. The study could also inform research for public health interventions, including antibiotic stewardship.

items.title: Large haploblocks underlie rapid, repeatable adaptation during evolutionary rescue
items.summary: Evolutionary rescue can prevent population extinction following abrupt environmental change, but the genetic architectures that enable rapid adaptation under simultaneous strong selection and severe demographic bottlenecks remain poorly resolved. In particular, rescue may rely on either dispersed adaptive variants or clusters of tightly linked alleles that can respond to selection despite strong…

research.abstract: Abstract Evolutionary rescue can prevent population extinction following abrupt environmental change, but the genetic architectures that enable rapid adaptation under simultaneous strong selection and severe demographic bottlenecks remain poorly resolved. In particular, rescue may rely on either dispersed adaptive variants or clusters of tightly linked alleles that can respond to selection despite strong drift. We investigated the genetic architecture of evolutionary rescue in Callosobruchus maculatus , the cowpea seed beetle, following a shift to lentil, a novel and stressful host. To do so, we combined experimental evolution, whole-genome sequencing, backcross introgression, early-generation genomic sampling, association mapping, and transcriptomics. Initial adaptation produced widespread genomic differentiation, but backcrossing localized evidence for adaptive variation primarily to large regions on chromosomes 1 and 9. These regions contained large haploblocks with patterns consistent with suppressed recombination, possibly due to structural variation. On chromosome 9, a rare haplotype increased from approximately 0.5% to 48% in a single generation in one genetic background, consistent with extremely strong selection ( s ≈ 0.9995). On chromosome 1, a 14 Mb haploblock contained nearly all genetic variation for two fitness-related traits and was associated with differential gene expression. Across genetic backgrounds, chromosome 1 was repeatedly implicated in adaptation, whereas lines from one source population additionally involved chromosome 9. Together, these results show that evolutionary rescue can rely on large, non-recombining haploblocks, providing a mechanism by which clustered genetic architectures can respond rapidly and repeatably despite severe population bottlenecks.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Synonymous codon usage bias (CUB) provides a complementary perspective on molecular variation, but its relationship with morphological diversity in rapidly radiating plant lineages remains poorly understood. We investigated this relationship in Thelypteridaceae by integrating chloroplast phylogenomics, codon usage analyses, and published descriptions of lamina base architecture. A phylogeny based on 31 shared protein‐coding genes provided the evolutionary framework for 37 plastome accessions, including two outgroups. Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) revealed three major codon usage groupings (Types A–C) that partly differed from the chloroplast phylogeny, with Types A and C corresponding descriptively to contrasting lamina base forms. A focused comparison of 27 accessions and eight genes retained this Type A–Type C separation. Although ENC, PR2, and neutrality plots showed broadly similar overall patterns between the types, gene‐wise analyses highlighted ndhJ, psaA, and psbD, and protein‐guided codon alignments reproduced their type‐specific synonymous third‐position counts. These complementary observations support a relationship between chloroplast codon usage variation and frond architecture in the sampled taxa. They identify candidate photosynthesis‐related loci and provide a basis for testing the evolutionary and functional processes underlying this relationship.

research.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infects the lungs and causes the disease tuberculosis, which the World Health Organization estimates causes 1 million deaths across the globe annually. Emergence of drug resistance has lessened the effectiveness and requires a longer duration of treatment. Bedaquiline was approved by the FDA in 2012 to treat multi-drug-resistant tuberculosis cases when no other treatment was viable. TBAJ-587, a derivative of Bedaquiline, has been found to be more effective at treating multi-drug-resistant tuberculosis, and has fewer adverse effects. The aim of this project was to test if strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis that have a mutation in Rv0678 causing overexpression of the MmpS5L5 efflux pump will evolve high-level resistance to TBAJ-587 at a higher frequency than wild-type strains. This was done by growing a wild-type M. tuberculosis strain and a ∆Rv0678 mutant on plates of 7H11 agar containing increasing concentrations of TBAJ-587, then selecting isolates and confirming resistance using an anti-microbial susceptibility assay to determine the Minimum Inhibitory Concentration of the isolated strains. 72 strains from the wild-type background were assayed, and 114 from the ∆Rv0678 background were assayed. The resistant ∆Rv0678 strains tended to have higher minimum inhibitory concentrations that the resistant WT strains. Mutations in the WT strains were found throughout Rv0678, and D28, E6, A62 and I66 mutations in atpE, as well as L168 in atpB. Similar atpE mutations were found in ∆Rv0678, with the addition of mutations in A63 of atpE.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Apolipoprotein B (apoB) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) are established biomarkers of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) that tend to be closely correlated. However, some individuals have discordant apoB and LDL-C. We evaluated whether apoB/LDL-C discordance is associated with elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), a key marker of systemic inflammation, in a nationally representative sample. Methods and Results We analyzed cross-sectional data of 2226 adults aged 20 years or older from the 2015 to 2016 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with complete apoB, LDL-C, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). LDL-C and apoB were converted to survey-weighted z scores, and discordance was the residual of apoB regressed on LDL-C. Participants were classified as apoB-high, LDL-C-high, or concordant (reference). The association of discordance group with elevated hs-CRP ( > 3 mg/L) was estimated with survey-weighted logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), and diabetes. Discordance was present in 26.4% of adults (13.7% apoB-higher, 12.6% LDL-C-higher). Elevated hs-CRP prevalence differed by discordance group: 47.6% (95% CI, 37.6–57.7) in the apoB-high group versus 20.5% (12.9–28.1) in the LDL-C-high group and 33.6% (29.7–37.4) in the concordant group. Relative to concordant participants, adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP were higher for apoB-high discordance (odds ratio [OR], 1.58; 95% CI, 1.03–2.45) and lower for LDL-C-high discordance (OR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.30–0.78). Similar results were obtained among participants not on statin therapy, with apoB-high discordance demonstrating stronger adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.01–4.04). Conclusion Discordantly high apoB relative to LDL-C is associated with systemic inflammation in a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults.

research.abstract: Abstract Cytochrome P450 (CYP) genes form a large and functionally diverse superfamily of heme-thiolate monooxygenases that catalyse the oxidation of endogenous and exogenous compounds. Within this superfamily, CYP4 enzymes primarily act on fatty acids, substrates central to energy metabolism. Sustained flight and long distance migration in birds rely on efficient fatty acid use, making CYP4 a pertinent system for examining how lipid associated functions may vary across avian lineages. Here, we characterised the evolution of CYP4 genes across 363 avian whole genomes, representing over 90% of bird families, to investigate patterns of molecular evolution and their association with ecological and life history variation. We identified four CYP4 subfamilies and analysed sequence evolution using site-models, branch-models, and branch-site models. Our analyses revealed conserved elements of the avian CYP4 repertoire alongside lineage-specific heterogeneity in selective constraint. Several amino acid sites under positive selection were located within substrate recognition sites, regions influencing substrate binding and catalysis. Branch-model analyses identified trait-associated variation in selective pressure across feeding habits, migration and primary lifestyle, with gene-specific patterns. Migration-associated differences in ω remained below one, indicating variation in the strength of selective constraint among migration categories. Branch-site analyses revealed evidence of episodic positive selection associated with migratory lineages. Overall, these results highlight site-specific adaptive evolution within CYP4 genes alongside broader variation in selective constraint, providing insight into the evolution of lipid associated metabolic pathways during avian diversification.

research.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Hepatic tuberculosis is a rare extrapulmonary manifestation that may mimic hepatobiliary malignancy or complex cystic lesions, resulting in diagnostic challenges. Case Presentation: A 36-year-old Filipino woman without recognized immunocompromising conditions presented with fever, weight loss, jaundice, and right upper quadrant pain. Imaging showed a multiloculated cystic lesion in hepatic segments V/VI with focal biliary prominence. Liver biopsy demonstrated necrotizing and non-necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with focally positive Ziehl-Neelsen staining. Tissue MTB-PCR detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis without rifampicin resistance, and culture confirmed M. tuberculosis complex susceptible to streptomycin, isoniazid, rifampicin, and ethambutol. CT chest showed diffuse bilateral micronodules in a miliary pattern; initial sputum smear and PCR were negative, but final sputum culture became positive at 6 weeks. Standard 2HRZE/4HR therapy was initiated, with clinical and biochemical improvement at 1 month. Conclusion: Hepatic tuberculosis should be considered in atypical cystic hepatic lesions, and tissue diagnosis is essential to avoid unnecessary invasive procedures.

research.abstract: Bacterial flagella are rotary nanomachines that enable motility in diverse environments. Although more than 40 genes are required for a functional flagellum in model organisms, only 24 have previously been inferred to be ancestral. Did the last bacterial common ancestor (LBCA) encode a simpler flagellum that was subsequently elaborated, or has its complexity been underestimated because highly diverged homologs are difficult to detect? Here, we combine homology searches across 80,789 bacterial proteomes with conserved sequence signatures, gene-tree clustering, and gene-neighborhood evidence to reconstruct the ancestral flagellum. We identify 49 flagellar protein groups with high-confidence support for ancestral presence across three phylogenetic reconstructions and one additional likely ancestral component, yielding a reconstructed repertoire of 50 ancestral protein groups. This repertoire includes the major structural, export, motor, and assembly components required for a functional flagellum. We provide an interactive database (https://www.flagelladb.org) for exploring the distribution, co-presence, and phylogenetic relationships of flagellar components across bacteria. Our findings indicate that the LBCA possessed a complex, functionally complete flagellar system, substantially exceeding previous estimates of ancestral complexity. The distribution of these components among extant bacteria is consistent with extensive lineage-specific loss and remodeling during subsequent flagellar evolution.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Riboflavin biosynthesis is required for in vitro survival of the human pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ). However, despite the lack of a known transporter, growth can be rescued by exogenous riboflavin. The riboflavin biosynthesis pathway is also predicted essential in vivo , but whether riboflavin levels available in the host can support survival has not been directly tested. Here we constructed a set of inducible CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) knockdown and targeted gene deletion strains for known riboflavin biosynthesis genes ( ribA2, ribG, ribH, ribC ) as tools to characterize riboflavin requirements, uptake, and metabolite changes and to assess in vivo essentiality. We found that riboflavin, but not flavin adenine dinucleotide or flavin mononucleotide, rescued auxotrophy for all strains tested. Further, riboflavin uptake was not affected by disruption of proton motive force or ATP synthesis, suggesting that uptake is not via an active mechanism. Targeted metabolite profiling after removal of riboflavin from growth medium confirmed reduced riboflavin levels. While other riboflavin intermediates were not detected, significant accumulation of aromatic amino acids (Phe, Tyr) was observed across all assayed strains, as well as alteration in a vitamin B9 metabolite. Selecting the ribC knockout as a representative strain, we found that riboflavin depletion had a bacteriostatic effect as late as 3 weeks after removal. Unexpectedly, Δ ribC lacked infectivity in an aerosol mouse infection, suggesting that the potential to scavenge riboflavin from the host is not sufficient to survive in vivo . Overall, our results show that altered metabolism upon loss of riboflavin biosynthesis leads to compromised Mtb infectivity. IMPORTANCE Tuberculosis remains one of the world’s most deadly infectious diseases, underscoring the need to explore new drug targets. Riboflavin (vitamin B2) biosynthesis has emerged as a promising target because Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ) depends on this pathway for survival. The riboflavin pathway also produces metabolites that modulate host mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cell activity, towards understanding potential strategies for host-directed therapies. Here we found that disrupting riboflavin biosynthesis led to not only compromised survival, but also widespread changes to metabolism and loss of the ability to establish infection in an animal model. These findings improve our understanding of how Mtb adapts to metabolic stress, with implications for developing drugs that target riboflavin biosynthesis and for alterations in host immunity to be explored in future studies.

research.abstract: BackgroundLinkage of infectious-disease surveillance data to mortality records is important for estimating long-term outcomes, but incomplete personal identifiers present methodological challenges. We developed and validated a deterministic linkage framework for linking the National Tuberculosis Surveillance System (NTBS) with Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality records. MethodsTB notifications in England from 2001-2024 were linked to ONS mortality records using 12 sequential matching rules based on combinations of NHS number, date of birth, name, postcode, sex and phonetic matching. Linkage outputs underwent person-level deduplication and clerical review. Precision and recall were estimated, and potential linkage bias assessed by variation in identifier completeness and linkage success. Confirmed false-positive links identified during validation were removed from the analytical dataset. ResultsAmong 151,965 TB notifications, 28,060 initial links were identified. Following deduplication, validation and refinement, 26,937 linked notifications were retained. Estimated precision increased from 97.7% to 99.2% (95% CI 96.8-100.0) following removal of false-positive links; estimated recall was 98.1% (95% CI 95.4-98.6%). More than 90% of links used NHS-number-based match keys. PDS enrichment increased NHS-number availability and enabled additional NHS-number-based links, although a small proportion linked to different ONS records following enrichment. NHS number availability and linkage success differed across demographic and social groups, demonstrating differential linkage. ConclusionsA hierarchical deterministic approach combined with targeted validation achieved high linkage accuracy while identifying and addressing differential linkage. This provides a transparent framework for future NTBS-ONS linkage and may be adaptable to other surveillance systems where comparable identifiers are available. research.abstract: Abstract Sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) can expand archaeological research by recovering broad biological signals from small amounts of sediment. Here, we apply shotgun sedaDNA metagenomics and target capture (also known as hybridization capture) to disused Roman wells from the vicus of Harelbeke, Belgium, dated to ca. 160-300 CE, and integrate the results with existing bioarchaeological datasets. Moving beyond individual introduced taxa as proxies for Roman influence, we reconstruct community-level profiles spanning consumption-related, synanthropic, and environmental organisms. SedaDNA reproduced most established bioarchaeological signals, including cultivated plants and domestic animals, while also recovering additional environmental taxa that established methods underrepresented. Mitochondrial target capture strengthened selected faunal detections and enabled phylogenetic placement of a pig ( Sus scrofa ) within the European mitochondrial lineage. The predominance of previously established consumption-related taxa is consistent with subsistence continuity and selective adoption of Roman-introduced resources, although taxon counts alone cannot establish their relative importance. Analytical-effort modeling further indicates that batch-based sedaDNA workflows can provide broad biological profiles at lower cost and time investment than established archaeological methods. Overall, sedaDNA complements conventional bioarchaeology by broadening taxonomic recovery, supporting scalable sampling, and providing a broad-spectrum approach to reconstructing settlement ecology, subsistence, and human-environment interaction.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD) frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic susceptibility and directional associations remain unclear. Methods We analyzed European-ancestry genome-wide association study (GWAS) data for ADHD (38,691 cases; 186,843 controls) and BPD (12,339 cases; 1,041,717 controls). Linkage disequilibrium score regression, conjunctional false discovery rate (conjFDR), bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR), MR accounting for linkage disequilibrium and sample overlap (MR-LAP), Causal Analysis Using Summary Effect estimates (CAUSE), colocalization, and Sum of Single Effects (SuSiE) fine-mapping assessed genetic sharing and directionality. Results Genetic correlation was substantial (r_g = 0.733). ConjFDR identified 48 shared loci; 36 (75%) showed concordant directions in both phenotype-specific comparisons. Functional annotation implicated axon guidance, oxidative phosphorylation, and developing midbrain cells. ADHD-to-BPD MR was positive (22 instruments; inverse-variance weighted beta = 0.487, SE = 0.082, p = 3.27 × 10^-9), persisting after outlier removal, MR-LAP correction, and exclusion of two instruments at colocalized loci. Reverse MR was positive (five instruments; beta = 0.303, SE = 0.112, p = 6.83 × 10^-3) but heterogeneous and variant-sensitive. CAUSE favored directional over sharing-only models in both directions (delta ELPD = 6.98 and 5.92, respectively). SuSiE colocalization supported shared signals at rs17576773, rs9969232, and rs4727799. Conclusions ADHD and BPD exhibit extensive genetic overlap involving 48 shared loci and convergent evidence of directional associations. Findings across complementary methods more consistently support an ADHD-to-BPD relationship, suggesting that shared genetic susceptibility alone may not fully explain their co-occurrence.

This study aimed to identify TB-associated ARG transcripts, characterize their immune and molecular correlates, and evaluate their exploratory diagnostic performance across prespecified cohorts. The local cohorts were selected using random sampling. Age-adjusted differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, machine-learning-based feature selection, immune-infiltration analysis, consensus clustering, single-cell annotation, and Comparative Toxicogenomics Database-based compound-gene screening were performed. Results GSE83456 included 45 TB patients and 61 controls. Age-adjusted differential expression identified 189 differentially expressed genes, and the intersection of DEGs, ARGs, and blue-module genes yielded 11 discovery candidates. Nested model selection in GSE83456 identified a naive Bayes classifier based on STAT1, PLAUR, JAK2, and P2RY14. Across five repeated stratified nested cross-validation runs, the mean AUC was 0.962, with a repeat-level range of 0.954-0.969. Balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 0.926, 0.911, 0.941, and 0.928, respectively. Exploratory evaluations included GSE19439, GSE34608, GSE62525, GSE19444, and the local RNA-seq cohort. CIBERSORT analysis identified significant TB-control differences in 9 of 22 inferred immune-cell types. CTD screening generated exploratory compound-gene associations that provide testable hypotheses for future experimental studies. research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the causative agent of tuberculosis (TB) is able to survive and replicate within host cells of the myeloid cell lineage, a critical step in the development of active TB, achieved through multiple immune evasion mechanisms. TRPML1 (Mucolipin 1), a non-selective Ca 2+ ion channel belonging to the TRP superfamily, is predominantly expressed in innate immune cells and is localized intracellularly along the endosomal-lysosomal continuum. TRPML1-mediated Ca 2+ signalling is vital for lysosomal biogenesis and trafficking processes essential for effective immune responses. The mechanisms regulating TRPML1 channel function in myeloid cells during mycobacterial infection remain poorly characterized. METHODS: During in vitro infection, TRPML1 expression was modulated in a time-dependent manner by Mtb and M. bovis BCG in murine macrophages, as well as in human neutrophils (PMNs) and macrophages (MDMs). Using pharmacological modulation of TRPML1 channel activity, we observed alterations in intracellular Ca 2+ concentrations following Mtb infection. RESULTS: Here, we describe distinct TRPML1 expression patterns in granulomas from TB patients who had completed treatment for active TB, suggesting a potential role for TRPML1 in pathogenesis. We further demonstrate that Mtb infection is associated with altered TRPML1 expression and intracellular Ca 2+ homeostasis, accompanied by changes in ROS production, necrotic cell death and enhanced mycobacterial survival within host cells. Treatment of PMN-MDM cocultures with a TRPML1 antagonist, but not an agonist, was associated with increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and necrotic cell death. DISCUSSION: Here, we show that Mtb-mediated disruption of TRPML1 function is associated with altered intracellular Ca 2+ homeostasis and may contribute to impaired phagosome maturation, a process previously linked to TRPML1-dependent endolysosomal function, thereby potentially favoring mycobacterial survival within host cells. These findings suggest that Mtb-induced alterations in TRPML1 associated cellular Ca²⁺ homeostasis may impair Ca²⁺-dependent ROS production and cell death, potentially affecting intracellular Mtb survival. Our findings support a role for TRPML1 in maintaining myeloid cell Ca²⁺ homeostasis and suggest that TRPML1 may contribute to the innate immune response to Mtb infection.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Tuberculosis (TB) notifications have increased in several high-income countries since 2020. Proposed explanations include pandemic-related disruption of treatment for latent tuberculosis, changes in population composition, and immune dysfunction following SARS-CoV-2 infection. We assessed whether TB presentations increased during the pandemic era and then tested whether community SARS-CoV-2 activity was followed by increased mycobacterial disease. Methods We conducted a population-based ecological time-series study of first TB- and nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM)-coded hospital, emergency-department and ambulatory-clinic presentations in the Greater Toronto–Hamilton Area Plus (GTHA+), Ontario (2024 population approximately 11.2 million), from April 2011 through March 2024. NTM served as a comparator because it shares diagnostic pathways with TB but differs epidemiologically. Negative-binomial projection and full-series models estimated pandemic-era changes under three alternative trend assumptions. Distributed lag non-linear models estimated cumulative rate ratios for standardized community viral activity over 0–12 weeks; sensitivity analyses extended the maximum lag to 26 and 52 weeks. Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were prespecified comparators; data for five additional viral exposures were obtained after the primary analysis was completed and analysed as exploratory comparisons. Results We identified 3,985 first TB-coded and 5,214 first NTM-coded acute-care presentations. Across six models, estimated pandemic-era TB increases ranged from 3% to 22%. No model suggested an increased in NTM. SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with TB (cumulative rate ratio per 1-SD increase over 0–12 weeks 0.909, 95% CI 0.822–1.006) or NTM (0.953, 0.868–1.047). No positive associations were identified in subgroup analyses or with maximum lags of 26 or 52 weeks. Influenza was not associated with either outcome. RSV was associated with TB and NTM; only the RSV–NTM association met the Bonferroni threshold among the prespecified comparisons, and no exploratory associations met the experiment-wide threshold. Conclusions We identified a modest pandemic-era increase in TB-coded acute-care presentations in Ontario, Canada, although its estimated size depended on assumptions about underlying trends. NTM-coded presentations did not increase. Community SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with subsequent TB or NTM presentations at lags of up to one year and did not provide a temporal explanation for the population-level TB increase. Individual-level effects cannot be excluded.

research.abstract: Abstract Infectious diseases continue to pose a global health challenge, intensified by antimicrobial resistance and limitations of pharmaceutical countermeasures. Nanotechnology offers a promising front against these barriers using intelligent, multifunctional systems. This review explores the convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), CRISPR gene editing, bacteriophage therapy, and immune modulation within the framework of second-generation nanoparticle therapeutics. AI-guided modelling enables predictive optimization of nanoparticle design on the basis of size, charge, and surface proteins, targeting specific pathogens and providing enhanced stability. Consequently, nanoparticles serve as precision nanocarriers and protective delivery vehicles for the CRISPR-Cas system, shielding nucleic acid cargo from enzymatic degradation and enabling targeted intracellular delivery via pH-responsive endosomal escape mechanisms. The nanoparticles not only provide protection but also enable tissue-targeting and infection-site-specific delivery of the CRISPR-Cas system, facilitating precise genome editing to reverse resistance in specific pathogens such as HIV and Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Phage nanoparticle hybrids further expand antimicrobial potency by enhancing phage stability, delivery, and host range. Moreover, engineered nanoparticles modulate the immune system via immunosuppressive and immunostimulant strategies for reducing hyperinflammation and enhancing pathogen clearance, respectively. Despite such encouraging laboratory outcomes, the clinical translation of AI-integrated nanoparticle platforms still faces a number of obstacles. Large-scale manufacturing, scalability, and reproducibility pose a significant challenge. Regulatory approvals for such multi-modal nano-drugs seem to get bogged down due to vague and scarce exemplary proofs. Furthermore, safety and efficacy apprehensions, unpredictable and complex host-phage interactions, cost-effectiveness, and equitable access remain a subject matter of concern. Conclusively, the convergence of advanced nanotechnology, artificial intelligence, and synthetic biology marks the dawn of a transformative era in infectious disease therapeutics where treatment is not only intelligent and adaptive but also ethically and globally inclusive. research.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prevalence and evolution of drug resistance in TB pose a persistent threat to global TB control. Understanding the epidemiological characteristics, population distribution, and temporal trends of drug resistance is crucial for evaluating the effectiveness of prevention and control measures and adjusting strategies accordingly. METHODS: This study retrospectively analyzed 9,665 clinical isolates of Mycobacterium TB collected between 2015 and 2024. Drug susceptibility testing was performed using the proportion method to detect resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, streptomycin, and levofloxacin. The chi-square test was used to compare differences between groups, and the chi-square test for trend was applied to analyze temporal changes in drug resistance. RESULTS: The overall drug resistance rate was 20.87% (2017/9665, 95% CI: 20.06%-21.69%), and the MDR rate was 10.25% (991/9665, 95% CI: 9.66%-10.88%). Drug resistance rates varied significantly among different populations, with males (1528/6730,22.70%; 95% CI: 21.71%-23.72%) exhibiting higher rates than females (489/2935,16.66%; 95% CI: 15.33%-18.06%), and the 19-59 age group (1511/6788,22.26%; 95% CI: 21.27%-23.27%) showing higher rates than the ≤ 18 (124/694,17.87%; 95% CI: 15.09%-20.92%) and ≥ 60 age groups (382/2183, 17.50%; 95% CI: 15.93%-19.16%). Over the ten-year period, the overall drug resistance rate showed a significant upward trend (from 17.29% to 22.98%). Rates of single drug resistance, PDR, and resistance to streptomycin and levofloxacin also increased significantly. In contrast, the MDR rate and resistance rates to rifampicin and ethambutol did not show significant trends. CONCLUSION: The TB drug resistance problem in this region is severe, with a rapid increase in resistance to the key second-line drug levofloxacin, indicating significant challenges for the current prevention and control system. Targeted interventions for populations with higher resistance rates, such as males and young adults, along with strengthened antibiotic stewardship, are critical to curbing the further spread of drug resistance.

research.abstract: Introduction TB incidence in Suriname has remained stable over the last decade. Understanding transmission patterns is essential for developing effective TB control strategies to interrupt ongoing transmission. Methods We conducted a descriptive analysis of routinely collected demographic and clinical data combined with whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data. Patients were classified into large (>6 patients) clusters, small (2-6 patients) clusters, or as non-clustered cases (unique). Bivariate and multivariable analyses compared patients in large clusters with those in small clusters and non-clustered patients. Epidemiological links obtained through patient interviews were compared with WGS findings. Results Of 698 TB patients notified during 2019-2024, WGS data were available for 368 (53%); 85% belonged to a genomic cluster. Indigenous ethnicity was inversely associated with membership in a large versus a small cluster (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.3; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.1-0.6). Compared with non-clustered cases, patients in large clusters were more likely to report illicit drug use (aOR = 3.0; 95% CI = 1.1-8.9). Conclusion WGS provided detailed insights into Mycobacterium tuberculosis transmission in Suriname. Illicit drug use was associated with membership in large transmission clusters, highlighting the need for early case finding and strengthened collaboration between TB and substance-use services.

research.abstract: A protein's sequence says what a gene could do in another species; the cells of that species say what it does there. Comparative genomics measures the first. Chimera measures the second, a gene's deployment, on the same genes and reports the difference. It aligns single-cell atlases across species in one generative model and returns, for every one-to-one ortholog, the evidence in the counts for a shared expression pattern, and {Delta}[a], the position of that evidence above or below what the protein's identity predicts. This difference is not sequence constraint under another name: across eight tissues, protein identity tracks dN/dS, whereas {Delta}[a] tracks neither. A gene therefore has two coordinates, not one, and the second can contradict the first: spermatocyte genes such as ZPBP2 keep their stage pattern on less conserved proteins, in eight held-out species, whereas conserved hepatocyte enzymes such as ALAS1 share their pattern but not their level. More broadly, genes of specialized cells sit above what their proteins predict in 23 of 24 cohorts, and approved drug targets do so more often than matched genes. Even among nearly identical proteins, where sequence can no longer tell genes apart, the count evidence still does. Nor does this rest on the model alone: independent data support the count evidence in liver and testis and, in a pre-specified test, {Delta}[a] in liver. With both coordinates, one can ask whether another species uses a gene as humans do, the premise of every animal model of a disease gene or drug target.

research.abstract: Ancestral sequences and substitution histories are usually averaged out in phylogenetic inference and are therefore not reported to the user. However, they can be recovered through ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) and stochastic character mapping. By implementing and validating a new ASR and stochastic mapping package compatible with both single-locus and multispecies coalescent analysis, we show how reconstructing substitution histories can enhance the information gained about the tempo and mode of molecular evolution. We observe that known substitution histories (simulated and empirical) are recovered more accurately and precisely on time trees compared with unconstrained and non-ultrametric substitution trees that lack temporal directionality (maximum likelihood and Bayesian). We show that codon-partition models with site-rate heterogeneity, based on the four nucleotide characters, can effectively approximate the histories of synonymous and non-synonymous change, while requiring far less runtime than computationally demanding codon models that require 61 characters. In turn, this provides low-bias estimation of dN/dS that is robust to non-stationarity in GC content, codon usage bias, and nucleotide exchangeability rates. Lastly, using three case studies, we demonstrate how the approach can recover expected patterns in molecular evolution and pathogen transmission: that i) smaller-bodied mammalian species tend to have faster synonymous substitution rates than larger relatives, ii) amino acid substitutions are correlated with 3Di structural changes in aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, and iii) influenza A virus spread more frequently to nearby locations than distant ones, in a major H3N2 outbreak in New Zealand. These three trends were more pronounced when based on count estimates derived from stochastic mapping, relative to parametric rates and distances. Our open-source code comes with a user-friendly graphical interface, as the BeastMap package for BEAST 2; supporting a wide range of clock, site, and tree models and data types - including insertions and deletions - within a Bayesian phylogenetic framework.

research.abstract: Abstract The rapid evolution of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) facilitates the emergence and fixation of drug-resistance mutations (DRMs). Although variants carrying DRMs gain a selective advantage under antiretroviral treatment, these mutations may compromise protein fitness, affecting viral replication efficiency and shaping evolutionary trajectories. Understanding the emergence, fixation, and fitness effects of DRMs is therefore essential for predicting evolutionary outcomes and optimizing therapies. Here, we investigated the evolution of the HIV-1 integrase, a key antiretroviral target, and the influence of common DRMs by analyzing folding stability, DNA substrate binding affinity, and structural properties across integrase variants using long molecular dynamics simulations combined with protein phylogenetic inference. DRMs generally altered protein folding stability and protein-DNA interactions to a marginal extent, due to their number, position, and physicochemical properties. Several DRMs altered catalytic site geometry, including alteration of magnesium coordination within the catalytic triad and modulation of enzymatic activity by changes in flexibility of the 140–149 loop involved in substrate binding, while others had minor effects on DNA binding. Over long evolutionary timescales, temporal fluctuations in folding stability and DNA-binding affinity were observed, potentially driven by alternating diversification and selection regimes at molecular and population levels. We conclude that HIV-1 integrase evolves under marginal stability, allowing structural variation that supports adaptation while preserving essential activity, which should be considered in predictions of structural evolutionary trajectories. Together, integrating biophysical properties with evolutionary modeling provides a robust framework for understanding how structural constraints influence the fixation of adaptive mutations. Statement Viral adaptation to antiretroviral therapies is a major health challenge. Understanding how HIV changes over time and develops drug resistance is essential for improving treatment strategies. Here, we studied HIV-1 integrase, an important target of antiretroviral drugs, and found that its drug-resistant variants can tolerate structural changes while maintaining their stability and function. This flexibility may help the virus adapt while preserving essential activity.

research.abstract: Abstract The cellular composition and spatial organization of immune responses within tuberculosis (TB) granulomas have been increasingly characterized, yet how these spatially organized immune cell populations coordinate local adaptive immunity remains largely unknown. Here, we integrated single-cell multi-omics, spatial transcriptomics, and immune receptor profiling to construct a comprehensive spatial atlas of human TB granulomas. We identified two concentric adaptive immune niches surrounding the central necrotic core. The outer niche comprised granuloma-associated tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) that supported T FH -B cell interactions and exhibited functional germinal center-like features associated with antigen-driven B-cell maturation toward FCRL5⁺ antibody-producing cells. The inner niche contained antigen-experienced and Mtb -reactive effector memory CD8⁺ T cells (T EM ), which were recruited from distal lung regions by LGALS9 high chemokine-expressing macrophages and activated to undergo local clonal expansion. In lgals9l1 deficient zebrafish, macrophage depletion was accompanied by marked reductions in T– and B-cell enrichment within granulomas and increased bacterial loads, supporting a role for LGALS9 high macrophages in coordinating local adaptive immunity against TB infection. Finally, AI-based prediction of spatial gene expression from clinical hematoxylin and eosin-stained specimens revealed that inferred TLS abundance increased with TB disease severity. These findings identify spatially interconnected adaptive immune niches that organize protective immune responses within human TB granulomas, therefore providing a foundation for understanding granuloma adaptive immunity and developing host-directed therapies and vaccines for TB ( https://tbomics.smart-nbc.org.cn/ ).

research.abstract: Abstract Neutrophils can promote pathogen control or drive tissue-damaging inflammation, but the mechanisms that determine these divergent outcomes remain poorly defined. COVID-19 and active tuberculosis (TB) offer a purposeful comparison since both are pulmonary infections with substantial neutrophil involvement, yet differ in pathogen class, inflammatory duration, and the balance between neutrophil-associated host defense and pathology. We therefore tested whether their divergent neutrophil programs align with distinct maturation-associated transcriptional states. We integrated six publicly available whole-blood bulk RNA-sequencing datasets, comprising three COVID-19 and three active TB cohorts. A curated panel of 770 genes covered activation, degranulation, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, chemotaxis, cell surface receptors, and maturation. Study-associated variation was reduced using ComBat-Seq, and differential expression relative to disease-appropriate controls was assessed with DESeq2. Most genes changed in the same direction in both diseases, but 348 (45.2%) differed significantly in response magnitude, with 159 genes showing a stronger response in COVID-19 and 189 in TB. COVID-19 samples showed reduced expression of the maturation markers CD10 ( MME ) and CD16 ( FCGR3A ), alongside elevated expression of granule-cargo and NET-associated genes, including MPO and ELANE , consistent with a greater contribution from immature, emergency granulopoiesis-derived neutrophil populations. In contrast, TB samples showed higher maturation-associated, receptor, oxidative, and recruitment responses, consistent with a relatively mature receptor-competent neutrophil transcriptional signature. Independent COVID-19 Ward and pulmonary TB cohorts showed directional agreement for maturation and NET-associated signatures (100% and 90% concordance, respectively), while chemotaxis and select receptor and degranulation genes showed weaker reproducibility indicating that maturation represents the most consistently reproduced axis of distinction between the two diseases. Together, these findings identify maturation-associated transcription as the most consistently reproduced axis distinguishing COVID-19 from TB. These signatures provide candidate biomarkers for future studies linking neutrophil states to clinical outcomes and informing host-directed therapeutic strategies that preserve antimicrobial function while limiting immunopathology.

research.abstract: Empyema necessitans is a rare complication of pleural infection in which infected pleural fluid extends through the parietal pleura into the surrounding soft tissues. We report the case of a 32-year-old man of Indian origin living in the United Kingdom who presented with worsening right-sided pleuritic chest pain, several months of night sweats, and a persistent dry cough. Five months earlier, he had been treated for right-sided pneumonia complicated by a pleural effusion, with persistent radiographic abnormalities on follow-up. Examination revealed reduced right-sided air entry and a tender, fluctuant swelling over the right posterior chest wall. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated a posterior pleural collection extending through the chest wall into the adjacent paraspinal musculature, consistent with empyema necessitans. Ultrasound-guided aspiration yielded frank purulent fluid. Routine bacterial, anaerobic, and fungal cultures were negative. Acid-fast bacilli were not seen on initial microscopy; however, mycobacterial culture became positive after seven days, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of the pleural fluid detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. Whole-genome sequencing subsequently identified a lineage 1 East-African-Indian-Ocean isolate with predicted susceptibility to first-line antituberculous agents. Four-drug antituberculous therapy was commenced, with subsequent clinical and radiological improvement. This case highlights chest wall swelling as an unusual presentation of tuberculosis and emphasizes the importance of cross-sectional imaging and targeted mycobacterial testing in establishing the diagnosis.

research.abstract: Polygonatum zanlanscianense Pamp. is a perennial herb (Asparagaceae) endemic to China, whose rhizomes are used in folk medicine as a substitute for Polygonati Rhizoma. Although its plastome has been reported, the mitogenome remained uncharacterized. Here, we assembled and annotated the complete linear mitogenome of P. zanlanscianense and analysed its gene repertoire, codon usage, repeats, RNA editing sites, MTPTs, synteny, phylogeny and Ka/Ks. The 689,491-bp mitogenome (GC 46.23%) encodes 56 genes: 36 PCGs, three rRNA genes and 17 tRNA genes. Codon usage is biased toward A/U-ending codons. We identified 68 SSRs, 25 tandem repeats, 1366 dispersed repeat pairs, 585 predicted C-to-U editing sites concentrated at the first and second codon positions, and 30 MTPT fragments accounting for 2.24% of the mitogenome. Phylogenetic analysis placed P. zanlanscianense as sister to Polygonatum kingianum Collett & Hemsl. Median Ka/Ks was below 1 for 33 of the 35 genes analysed; although rpl5 and ccmB showed elevated ratios, branch-site tests did not support positive selection. This first mitogenome of P. zanlanscianense provides genomic resources for comparative genomic, phylogenetic and medicinal studies in Polygonatum.

The study identify determinants of tuberculosis diagnosis delay among patients attending public health facility of Metekel zone, Northwest Ethiopia:2023 Methods An unmatched case-control study was conducted in Metekel zone health facilities from March to April 2023, involving 210 tuberculosis patients (103 cases, 107 controls) selected through systematic sampling. Data collected through structured questionnaires and STATA used for analysis, including bi-variable and multi-variable logistic regressions. Variables with p-value < 0.25 in bi-variable analysis were included in the final model after checking model fitness and multicollinearity. Results Overall, 210 tuberculosis patients were included in the study. The following independent variables were associated diagnosis delay of tuberculosis: TB patients who travel greater than 10km (AOR: 2.941, (95 % CI: 1.509, 5.731); TB patients who are living at rural area (AOR: 4.135, 95 % CI :1.759, 9.723); TB patients who prior visit in holly-water and traditional medicine [AOR: 2.978, (95% CI: 1.292, 6.863); poor knowledge about TB [AOR: 2.826, (95% CI: 1.404, 5.687)]. Conclusion Tuberculosis diagnosis delay is a major challenge to eliminate tuberculosis by breaking the chain of transmission. This study can be attributed to factors including place of residence being rural, poor knowledge about tuberculosis, non-health facility initial actions upon symptom onset, and far distance to health institutions. Recognizing these determinants helps in identifying and addressing barriers inhibiting early diagnosis, potentially improving healthcare access and promoting more timely diagnosis and treatment for tuberculosis patients.

research.abstract: Importance: Standard repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation protocols are difficult to integrate into inpatient psychiatric care because they require daily treatment over several weeks. Accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) may offer a feasible augmentation strategy for hospitalized patients with treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Objective: To determine whether connectivity-guided accelerated iTBS improves depressive symptoms beyond routine multimodal inpatient care in hospitalized patients with TRD. Design, Setting, and Participants: This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial was conducted in the inpatient unit of the Department of Psychiatry, University of Oldenburg, Karl-Jaspers-Klinik, Bad Zwischenahn, Germany. Patients aged 18 to 65 years with unipolar TRD were recruited between May 2021 and August 2024. Interventions: Participants received active or sham iTBS targeting an individualized left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex site showing strongest functional anticorrelation with the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex using resting-state functional MRI. Treatment was delivered as 3 daily sessions over 10 weekdays (30 sessions; 54 000 pulses total) as augmentation to routine multimodal inpatient care. Main Outcomes and Measures: Primary and secondary outcomes were changes in Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) scores assessed weekly and Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II) scores assessed daily during the 2-week stimulation phase. Exploratory outcomes included response and remission rates. Results: Of 57 randomized participants, 51 completed treatment (active, n=27; sham, n=24). The cohort exhibited moderate-to-severe treatment resistance (mean Maudsley Staging Method score, 10.9) and psychiatric comorbidity in 82% of participants. Active iTBS was associated with steeper MADRS improvement than sham (-3.54 points/week; 95% CI, -5.53 to -1.55; false discovery rate-adjusted P<.001), corresponding to model-estimated reductions of 12.06 versus 4.98 points (Cohen d=-0.89). BDI-II trajectories similarly favored active treatment, although with a smaller effect size (-0.23 points/day; 95% CI, -0.41 to -0.05; false discovery rate-adjusted P=.02; Cohen d=0.22). MADRS response rates were higher with active iTBS (42.3% vs 13.0%), whereas remission rates were numerically but not significantly greater (26.9% vs 12.5%). No serious adverse events occurred. Conclusions and Relevance: Accelerated connectivity-guided iTBS produced significant add-on antidepressant effects during acute inpatient treatment of TRD. Larger multicenter trials are needed to establish durability and optimize clinical implementation. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04832750 .

research.abstract: Multidrug efflux pumps are major drivers of antimicrobial resistance, but overlapping resistance mechanisms mask the physiological limits of efflux alone. Bacterial genomes encode a large repertoire of multidrug efflux pumps, which could theoretically combine to achieve exceptionally high levels of resistance. To delineate the extent of resistance achievable through efflux driven adaptation, we performed adaptive laboratory evolution of Mycobacterium smegmatis mc²155 wild-type and efflux-deleted (ΔlfrA, ΔefpA) strains against ethidium bromide, a broad-spectrum efflux substrate. Despite prolonged selection, resistance reproducibly plateaued at 8-16 fold increase in MIC under the tested conditions. This plateau emerged through distinct evolutionary trajectories characterized by non-overlapping efflux pump sets: from overexpression of the well-characterized lfrA to upregulation of multiple uncharacterized pumps, all conferring cross-resistance. Genetic reconstruction of mutations in a transcriptional regulator and a membrane protein, together with overexpression of efflux pumps, recapitulated the resistance phenotypes of the evolved strains. Sustained pump overexpression depleted membrane potential and drove metabolic suppression, suggesting that energetic exhaustion may constrain further increase in efflux-mediated resistance. Similar constraints were observed in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, indicating that they may extend to other mycobacterial species. Efflux-metabolic integration thus affects resistance evolution, revealing therapeutic vulnerabilities to combat multidrug resistance.

research.abstract: Microbial culture collections and synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) are essential experimental resources for investigating underlying mechanisms of plant-microbe interactions. However, such resources remain scarce for agriculturally relevant crops. Here, we address this gap by developing TriMic, a community resource to investigate plant-microbe interactions in wheat. We employed a host-mediated isolation approach to obtain a bacterial collection from wheat roots and characterized its taxonomic representation and functional potential through whole-genome sequencing. We further evaluated the community dynamics of a consortium derived from this collection across time and wheat genotypes to inform the selection of a simplified community. TriMic includes core and keystone taxa reported in previous wheat microbiomes studies. Moreover, genomic analysis revealed genetic potential for diverse genes associated with plant colonization, nutrient cycling, plant growth promotion, and biosynthetic gene clusters with taxa exhibiting metabolic patterns associated with both generalist and specialist strategies. The proposed 15-member SynCom reflects the taxonomic and functional relevance of the full collection. By integrating publicly accessible bacterial isolates, whole-genome sequences, and an ecologically informed SynCom, TriMic provides a foundation for translating ecological and genomic observations into testable hypotheses, advancing mechanistic investigations of microbial community assembly and plant-microbiome interactions.

research.abstract: Retrospective reassessment of archival brain banks provides opportunities to identify previously undocumented neuropathologies. However, limited tissue availability and preservation, together with differences in sampling and staining protocols across brain banks, can constrain the histological information available for analysis. This study investigated whether computational models can integrate complementary information across histological stains and retain discriminative information under incomplete stain availability. A deep learning model incorporating shared-specific feature modeling, cross-stain knowledge distillation, and random modality masking was developed and evaluated on 1,607 whole slide images from the dorsolateral frontal cortex of 602 donors across three cohorts. Using chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) and their comorbidity as a proof-of-principle application, our model achieved macro-averaged areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.899, 0.904, and 0.898 across three stain-defined groups, exceeding corresponding single-stain baselines. Discriminative performance was retained when each group's defining stain was withheld. Model-predicted disease probabilities were associated with neuropathological staging measures for AD and CTE, and spatial attribution patterns on the remaining stains were largely preserved under defining-stain masking. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of leveraging complementary and partially overlapping histopathological information under incomplete stain availability, providing a foundation for future computational studies across brain regions and brain banks.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Chronic exposure to environmental contaminants can drive population decline but also exert selective pressure favouring adaptive molecular responses that mitigate toxicity. Australian lead (Pb) mining and smelting towns provide a natural experiment to study such contemporary adaptation in the house sparrow ( Passer domesticus ), an invasive commensal species that has persisted in heavily contaminated environments for over a century. The Broken Hill population is of particular interest as it has remained geographically isolated with limited gene flow, whereas the Port Pirie population is connected to surrounding regions. Here, we used data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry to compare the blood and liver proteomes of wild-caught sparrows from both towns and identify divergent molecular responses to lead. Lead exposure altered the mitochondrial proteome and disrupted RNA splicing in both populations, but the two towns diverged sharply in haem biosynthesis and protein quality control. We identified a mechanistic cascade in which lead inhibits ALAD, depleting intracellular haem, stabilising the transcriptional repressor BACH1, and suppressing globin expression. Broken Hill birds maintained ALAD abundance, upregulated proteasomal subunits (PSMC) and HSP70 family chaperones, and preserved significantly higher haemoglobin concentrations despite equivalent blood lead levels. Port Pirie birds exhibited ALAD collapse, BACH1 accumulation, and reliance on autophagy rather than active protein quality control. Liver proteomics confirmed tissue-level convergence of the haem pathway disruption. Together, these findings reveal that over a century of isolation under sustained lead exposure has shaped population-specific molecular strategies in Broken Hill sparrows, with enhanced proteostasis and preserved haem biosynthesis representing signatures of local adaptation.

research.abstract: Small lytic phages of the ssRNA Leviviricetes and ssDNA Microviricetes achieve host lysis by expression of a single protein, designated as an Sgl protein. Four ssRNA Sgls have been shown to inhibit steps in peptidoglycan biosynthesis: three target MurJ, the Lipid II flippase, and one targets MurA, the committed step of the pathway. A fifth Sgl, the E protein of the canonical ssDNA microvirus {varphi}X174, inhibits MraY, which catalyzes the synthesis of the first lipid-linked intermediate. This inhibition requires SlyD, a cytoplasmic FKBP-type peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase. The Sgl of the Caulobacter ssRNA phage {varphi}Cb5 (Cebevirus halophobicum) has not been characterized. Here, we present physiological evidence that Sgl{varphi}Cb5 targets MraY. Moreover, we show that, despite the absence of detectable sequence similarity, Sgl{varphi}Cb5 shares several features with the {varphi}X174 E protein, including the distribution of hydrophobic and charged residues, a proposed N-out, C-in membrane topology, and retention of lytic activity in an Sgl{varphi}Cb5 -LacZ fusion. Furthermore, expression of the Caulobacter cytoplasmic FKBP-type peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase CC2799 enhances Sgl{varphi}Cb5 -mediated lysis in E. coli. These parallels between Sgl function in a DNA phage and an RNA phage either represent remarkably consonant convergent evolution or some evolutionary cross-over event for which there is currently no precedent.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Mycobacterium tuberculosis contains thirteen Mycobacterial membrane protein Large (MmpL) transporters, which belong to the family of secondary active RND transporters. MmpL4 and MmpL5, together with their operon partners MmpS4 and MmpS5, export the mycobacterial siderophore mycobactin and the last resort TB drug bedaquiline. Recently, we determined a structure of the MmpL4 monomer in complex with desferrated mycobactin, which lacked a functionally essential coiled-coil domain predicted to extend far into the periplasm. Here, we present a cryo-EM structure of the hexameric (MmpS4) 3 -(MmpL4) 3 complex, which was enabled by rational disulfide cross-links based on AlphaFold predictions. We observed density for the coiled-coil domain, which protrudes into the periplasmic space at an angle of around 60° relative to the symmetry axis of the MmpL4 trimer. In the context of the hexameric complex, MmpL4’s conformation differs strikingly from the one observed for monomeric MmpL4, which includes formation of a large cavity in the periplasmic domain and rearrangements of conserved proton coupling residues at the transmembrane domain. Two of the cross-linked variants were found to be functionally defective, indicating that the hexameric complex undergoes substantial conformational changes to accomplish mycobactin and drug transport.

research.abstract: SUMMARY Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading infectious cause of death, with drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) challenging disease control. Brazil has a high TB burden, and Rio Grande do Sul state reports persistently high incidence and drug-resistance rates. The drivers shaping the regional DR-TB burden remain poorly characterised. Methods We conducted genomic surveillance of confirmed DR-TB cases in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, from January 2023 to September 2024. Clinical isolates underwent genotypic (gDST) and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (pDST) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS). We analyzed 33 newly sequenced genomes and 267 historical Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes collected in 2011–2019 to characterize resistance, transmission, and spatiotemporal patterns and estimate the contributions of transmitted and acquired rifampicin resistance. Findings Molecular testing detected rifampicin resistance missed by pDST, including borderline rpoB mutations in 18.2% and emerging resistance-associated variants in 3% of the 33 analyzed isolates. Conversely, pDST detected baseline bedaquiline resistance missed by WGS in one newly diagnosed case. Among 300 genomes, 181 (60.3%) clustered into 32 genomic clusters at a 5-SNP threshold, including 12 with long-term circulation and several spanning prisons and communities. Sublineage frequencies remained stable over time, whereas we observed marked geographic structuring and localized clonal expansion. Among 178 rifampicin-resistant isolates, transmission accounted for an estimated 79.2–88.2% of resistance, corresponding to 11.8–20.8% of cases arising through de novo acquisition during treatment. Interpretation Our findings identify active transmission as the main driver of rifampicin-resistant TB in Rio Grande do Sul, with long-term transmission chains extending across both incarcerated and community settings. These results underscore the urgent need to strengthen timely TB case detection and resistance testing, enhance contact investigations, and implement targeted interventions aiming to interrupt persistent transmission chains.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Ghana, where GeneXpert MTB/RIF serves as a first–line diagnostic tool. However, uncertainties about this method persist regarding specimen quality and the clinical significance of indeterminate rifampicin susceptibility results. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross–sectional study of samples from 3,977 presumptive TB patients tested either at HopeXchange Medical Center (Kumasi) or Keta Municipal Hospital between January 2020 and December 2024. Demographic data, sputum macroscopic appearance, and GeneXpert results were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Fisher’s exact test. Results Overall Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTb) test positivity was 11.6% (461/3977). Males accounted for 63.3% of positive results, with the highest percentage among those ages 30–40 years. Mucopurulent specimens yielded the highest positivity rate (25.4%), compared to 4.0% of salivary specimens. Blood–stained sputum specimens (n=44) showed a 15.9% positivity rate. Although confirmed rifampicin resistance was low (1.7%), 9.3% of all MTb positive samples yielded an indeterminate result. The rate of indeterminate results from samples collected at Kwadaso Municipal increased from 7.3% in 2021 to 28.6% in 2024. Conclusion These findings validate Ghana National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) guidelines emphasizing the reliability of mucopurulent specimen collection, but challenges the routine rejection of blood–stained sputum. The rising trend of indeterminate rifampicin results requires further investigation of circulating rpoB mutation profiles and quality assurance measures. Patients with indeterminate results should be further assessed using drug susceptibility testing to rule out rifampicin resistance. The findings provide actionable evidence to refine diagnostic algorithms and improve TB care in Ghana.
